collection_form.title: Drosophila odorant receptor calcium-reporter platform
collection_form.description: A 25-part platform for exploring cellular odor sensing: ten Drosophila tuning-receptor CDSs, ten OR-IRES-mCherry modules, a GCaMP6f-Orco fusion and four fusion components. The design combines interchangeable tuning receptors with a shared calcium reporter in mammalian cells. Documentation connects sequence sources and architecture diagrams to labelled colony plates, undigested DNA gels, fixed-cell fluorescence and two separately documented exploratory plate batches. Measured conditions include exact image-object denominators, threshold sensitivity, within-stage fluorescence changes, baseline-drift subtraction, vehicle comparisons and untransfected controls. Basic components were not tested independently. The records support reuse of the design and analysis, but do not yet establish receptor specificity, membrane localization or a validated detection limit.

entries.title: A modular receptor–reporter architecture for exploring cellular odor sensing
entries.body_markdown:
The collection contains **25 parts**: ten tuning-receptor CDSs, ten corresponding OR-IRES-mCherry modules, one GCaMP6f–Orco fusion and its four components. It allows another team to evaluate a related fluorescence system while seeing which evidence is available and which claims remain untested.

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This motivates co-expressing a tuning-receptor module with the shared reporter fusion. The design separates an interchangeable receptor sequence from a common reporter architecture; it does not establish equivalent expression, localization or sensing performance after each substitution.

| Design choice | Intended role | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Human codon-adapted receptor DNA | Support mammalian expression | Team synthesis records; no matched native-codon comparison |
| OR–IRES–mCherry | Express receptor and marker as separate proteins | Red fluorescence is not a receptor abundance or localization assay |
| GCaMP6f–linker–Orco | Couple a calcium indicator to the co-receptor | Exploratory fluorescence; no independent localization proof |
| GCCACC on composites | Provide a mammalian initiation context | Sequence feature, not a comparative translation assay |
| No promoter or polyadenylation element | Let the host vector supply transcriptional control | Assembly must preserve start, frame and termination |
| Basic and composite versions | Permit reuse at different assembly levels | Basic components were not independently characterized |

Team records describe synthesis by GenScript in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Native reference protein and human codon adaptation describe intended design, not verification of every experimental plasmid. Individual CDS pages retain FlyBase gene/transcript identifiers, RefSeq accession and reference length. Component pages identify GCaMP6f, the synthetic linker and vector-derived RSET leader.

The stable-cell study of Zboray et al. is relevant prior art [2]. Its Orco was codon-optimized, whereas its tuning-receptor sequences were not; it should not be described as an entirely wild-type-DNA platform. Our transient cultures, expression arrangement and acquisition method differ. These data do not isolate an advantage from codon adaptation, linker length or IRES layout.

### How the parts are used together

A sensing condition combines one tuning-receptor module with the shared reporter–co-receptor fusion. The tuning receptor supplies the variable recognition component; the IRES-mCherry segment supplies a separate expression-associated marker. The fusion supplies the common calcium-sensitive optical readout. This separation lets a user replace the tuning receptor without redesigning the reporting construct, while testing whether the new combination actually expresses and responds.

![Example tuning-module design](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/1e5d35498251bd9b989a0ee41bd4a2a24016970ab2acf05d74c82e94b505ab1f.svg)

*Or7a illustrates the interchangeable OR-IRES-mCherry arrangement. It encodes two separate proteins. This is a design schematic, not a measurement of receptor localization or stoichiometry.*

![Shared reporter–co-receptor fusion design](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/ef416bf396dd17c80f5cf652ae9bcd21d5a3c0956e4624fdb0157c4a4a6296b6.svg)

*The RSET–GCaMP6f–(GGGGS)₃–DmOrco arrangement is shared by the ten sensing conditions. The four basic components allow the individual sequence elements to be reused; their separate presence in the collection does not mean they were independently tested.*

There are three distinct questions in the evidence below: was a labelled DNA preparation obtained; is localized reporter-associated fluorescence detectable in fixed cells; and how do later fluorescence changes compare with handling and biological-background controls? Success at one stage does not answer the next. The following records make the measured stage and the unresolved transition visible.

### Ligand panel and assembly

P2 includes VUAA1, six VOCs and a buffer-only row. VUAA1 is a literature-supported Orco agonist [3]. Zboray et al. used 2-heptanone as an Or85b reference compound. Their Or98a reference, 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one, is absent from P2. DoOR 2.0 can inform ligand selection [4], but its normalized measurements are not quantitative predictions for this HEK293 assay. A complete receptor-specific rationale for the supplied panel is not documented.

All 25 identifiers were returned as **published** by the official Registry API on 19 October 2026. The index records lengths and a motif scan. Many sequences contain internal restriction sites; the collection is not uniformly compatible with a single restriction-based standard. A motif-free result alone does not certify compatibility: flanking sequence, overhang design, reading frame, vector and the standard also matter. This read-only review did not change Registry records.

entries.title: Evidence provenance, paired fluorescence measurements and control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Construction and microscopy

The cloning record contains three colony photographs and four undigested plasmid gels. DNA is visible in **24 sample lanes**, two for each of **12 construct labels**, with similar migration within each pair. This supports DNA presence, not insert identity or restriction-fragment size. Uncut plasmid conformation affects migration. Colony growth identifies candidates for further checks, not successful assembly or sensor function.

The endpoint HEK293 image set contains **25 fields across 12 conditions**, with one to three fields per condition, around **44–48 h post-transfection**, before G418 selection, after **2% PFA fixation** and DAPI staining without documented permeabilization. Analysis pools eligible resolvable DAPI objects and reports RED-, GREEN- and dual-positive fractions at a blank-derived p99 cutoff; p95 and p99.5 sensitivity outputs are retained. Eligible objects cover only a subset of DAPI foreground. These fractions are not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability; fields are not independent biological repeats. Image-to-P2 batch identity is unresolved.

### Construction evidence and condition map

The three original colony photographs cover ten tuning-receptor labels and two reporter/co-receptor-related labels. Photographs 1–3 and gels A–D are reused directly from the existing official image assets, without new image synthesis or selective lane reconstruction.

![Construction photograph 1](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/b835aea2c8ee8e6b5b62185de0b2658505b74c668383c951201f01ce1bcd5842.avif)

*Photograph 1: Or22a upper-left, GCaMP6f-related handwritten label upper-right, Or85b lower-left and Or35a lower-right. The upper-right label does not establish the complete fusion identity.*

![Construction photograph 2](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/e6e2ea9316967ca9ad9b042663950d4844f7b9e7cdc1389967ba977894e56e9f.avif)

*Photograph 2: Or67a upper-left, Or19a upper-right, Or59b lower-left and Or42a lower-right. Visible colonies and marked picks are preparation records, not sequence verification.*

![Construction photograph 3](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/e87a937b275c7dcf7cf3f5b8cfda4f450e2cb7711a9d8200ccd10d3c1179b7d2.avif)

*Photograph 3: ORCO upper-left, Or67b upper-right, Or98a lower-left and Or7a lower-right. Full photographs preserve neighbouring plates and original labels; differences in colony density are not compared as transformation efficiencies.*

| Label | Colony photograph / plate position | Gel / sample lanes | Later fixed-cell condition | P2 column |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Or7a | 3 / lower-right | D / 1–2 | Or7a+ORCO | 1 |
| Or19a | 2 / upper-right | D / 5–6 | Or19a+ORCO | 2 |
| Or42a | 2 / lower-right | D / 7–8 | Or42a+ORCO | 3 |
| Or98a | 3 / lower-left | D / 9–10 | Or98a+ORCO | 4 |
| Or22a | 1 / upper-left | C / 1–2 | Or22a+ORCO | 5 |
| Or67a | 2 / upper-left | D / 3–4 | Or67a+ORCO | 6 |
| Or67b | 3 / upper-right | A / 3–4 | Or67b+ORCO | 7 |
| Or59b | 2 / lower-left | C / 3–4 | Or59b+ORCO | 8 |
| Or85b | 1 / lower-left | B / 3–4 | Or85b+ORCO | 9 |
| Or35a | 1 / lower-right | B / 1–2 | Or35a+ORCO | 10 |
| ORCO | 3 / upper-left | A / 1–2 | ORCO only (reporter fusion) | 11 |
| GCaMP6f-related label | 1 / upper-right | B / 5–6 (GCaMP6f) | No separate free-GCaMP6f condition | — |
| Untransfected | Not applicable | Not applicable | blank (no transfect) | 12 |

*This is correspondence between source labels, not a verified colony-to-assay lineage. Gel numbering excludes ladders. In particular, the ORCO/GCaMP6f construction labels do not establish whether a standalone or fused sequence was present.*

![Undigested plasmid gel A](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/b9b2e651fab271e8008d7469f3036023f8237d7367a9753ae9740c4e5c33e2ad.avif)

*Gel A: ORCO sample lanes 1–2 and Or67b 3–4.*

![Undigested plasmid gel B](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/47e61e3af7196df63c289375716b7b0377eaf0c90d32b7eec887fdb9ab72999b.avif)

*Gel B: Or35a 1–2, Or85b 3–4 and GCaMP6f 5–6.*

![Undigested plasmid gel C](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/1fd264b2e80144ae9856ce7d95228b9642449a4def86505e3e371b84b0f60f3e.avif)

*Gel C: Or22a 1–2 and Or59b 3–4.*

![Undigested plasmid gel D](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/753117eef1703875a3cf9e381b5fd7744678ff9b940f958714ae6c3022f33ac6.avif)

*Gel D: Or7a 1–2, Or67a 3–4, Or19a 5–6, Or42a 7–8 and Or98a 9–10, with ladders at both ends. Across all four gels, the preserved processing is rigid orientation and contiguous cropping, without lane splicing or intensity adjustment. The source-manifest records original TIFF hashes and the lane map.*

### Test 1: paired-round preparation and acquisition

P2 is one HEK293 plate at approximately **72 h post-transfection**, without G418 selection. Columns 1–10 are Or7a, Or19a, Or42a, Or98a, Or22a, Or67a, Or67b, Or59b, Or85b and Or35a, each with the fusion. Column 11 is reporter fusion alone; column 12 is **untransfected cells**, not cell-free buffer. Each condition–stimulus combination has one well. Raw headers span **10–11 October 2026**; team confirmation on 11 October does not make this a one-day acquisition.

Confirmed buffer: **140 mM NaCl, 5 mM KCl, 2 mM CaCl₂, 1 mM MgCl₂, 5 mM HEPES-Na and 20 mM glucose, pH 7.3, 340 mOsm**. VUAA1 was prepared in DMSO; final solvent fraction is unknown. VOCs were initially supplied in aqueous solution and diluted in buffer, but stock and final molar concentrations are unresolved. Plain buffer is not a documented matched vehicle for VUAA1.

CSV exports verify **482 ± 8 nm excitation / 530 ± 20 nm emission**, five-point baseline runs and 15-point response runs at **12-second cycles**, with response timestamps **0–168 s**. Four stages define each stimulus row: F0a, blank, F0b and test. Each response is normalized to its paired baseline.

The report identifies a BMG CLARIOstar Plus, GREINER 96F bottom plate, bottom optics, LP504, −4.1 mm focal setting, 20 flashes, 0.5 s settling and enhanced dynamic range off. It describes 50 µL additions, taking volume from 100 to 150 to 200 µL, with an eight-channel pipette for columns 1–8 then 9–12. These are report-level details, not settings independently recovered from CSVs. Numeric gain, addition-to-read delay, actual temperature and extent of reported detachment are unresolved. Nominal final VUAA1 is **50 µM** in the report, not independently confirmed by stock-preparation records. These data do not support dose–response or EC₅₀ estimates.

### Calculation and exclusions

F0 is each well's five-point paired-baseline mean. The peak statistic is the largest mean of three consecutive response readings. With normalized changes ΔFblank and ΔFtest:

- **R(s,c) = ΔFtest(s,c) − ΔFblank(s,c).** Original ΔFcorr, retained as the base fluorescence difference.
- **B(s,c) = R(s,c) − R(H,c).** H is the separate buffer-only well in the same column/condition.
- **D(s,c) = B(s,c) − [R(s,12) − R(H,12)].** Column 12 is untransfected cells under the same stimulus; H12 is its buffer reference.

R is dimensionless: 0.10 is a difference of normalized changes, not a ten-percent cell fraction. B and D add different-well controls. Buffer-row B and D, and untransfected-column D, are zero algebraically. Shared reference wells make contrasts dependent.

Rows **B (ethyl propionate)** and **C (isopentyl acetate)** are excluded following reported gain changes. All 96 wells and quality flags remain archived: **72 retained, 24 excluded**. Numeric gain is unavailable, so “retained” means exploratory, not verified constant-gain acquisition. Figure omission or hatching does not reinstate exclusions.

Earlier thresholds, including a roughly **0.13448** three-SD heuristic from six untransfected retained rows, remain only in the historical audit. Those rows represent different stimuli, not independently repeated blanks. Current tables do not classify responses using this heuristic, a first-point fraction or the earlier multi-rule acceptance test. B and D do not create replication or resolve missing solvent controls.

entries.title: Retained Test 1 measurements and the effect of between-well controls
entries.body_markdown:
**Assay labels.** Test 1 is the earlier four-acquisition experiment (archive label P2). Its plot labels “round 1” and “round 2” mean the buffer and test stages within Test 1; neither means Test 2. Test 1 tables retain dimensionless R/B/D values (multiply by 100 for percentage points). [Test 2](#odor-2026-10-21-methods) is the separate later two-acquisition experiment, with endpoint S in percentage points and construct-matched VUAA1 reference N.

### Fixed-cell expression-associated signal

The image analysis asks whether localized RED and GREEN fluorescence can be distinguished from the blank within resolvable nuclear neighbourhoods. It does not estimate a culture-wide transfection percentage. The following table supplies the exact eligible-object denominators so that a small numerator is not hidden by a rounded percentage.

| Condition | Technical fields | Eligible objects | Eligible DAPI foreground | RED-positive p99 | GREEN-positive p99 | Both-positive p99 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| blank (no transfect) | 3 | 170 | 9.1% | 1/170 (0.6%) | 1/170 (0.6%) | 1/170 (0.6%) |
| Or19a+ORCO | 2 | 242 | 16.2% | 25/242 (10.3%) | 1/242 (0.4%) | 0/242 (0.0%) |
| Or22a+ORCO | 2 | 189 | 9.9% | 8/189 (4.2%) | 1/189 (0.5%) | 1/189 (0.5%) |
| Or35a+ORCO | 2 | 200 | 10.2% | 28/200 (14.0%) | 11/200 (5.5%) | 8/200 (4.0%) |
| Or42a+ORCO | 2 | 263 | 22.8% | 18/263 (6.8%) | 4/263 (1.5%) | 1/263 (0.4%) |
| Or59b+ORCO | 2 | 230 | 21.1% | 38/230 (16.5%) | 3/230 (1.3%) | 2/230 (0.9%) |
| Or67a+ORCO | 2 | 161 | 10.6% | 17/161 (10.6%) | 6/161 (3.7%) | 4/161 (2.5%) |
| Or67b+ORCO | 2 | 193 | 9.5% | 14/193 (7.3%) | 2/193 (1.0%) | 2/193 (1.0%) |
| Or7a+ORCO | 2 | 192 | 16.2% | 21/192 (10.9%) | 3/192 (1.6%) | 1/192 (0.5%) |
| Or85b+ORCO | 1 | 156 | 18.9% | 25/156 (16.0%) | 8/156 (5.1%) | 7/156 (4.5%) |
| Or98a+ORCO | 2 | 286 | 20.2% | 2/286 (0.7%) | 2/286 (0.7%) | 2/286 (0.7%) |
| ORCO only | 3 | 342 | 19.6% | 0/342 (0.0%) | 24/342 (7.0%) | 0/342 (0.0%) |

The two channels answer different questions: mCherry is an independent expression-associated marker, while GREEN signal is associated with the reporter fusion. The fusion-only condition lacks mCherry; it retains 24 GREEN-positive objects but no RED-positive objects at p99. Or98a has only two objects above either p99 cutoff despite a much higher count at p95. These differences motivate showing threshold sensitivity rather than reporting a single apparent efficiency.

![Microscopy threshold sensitivity and dual-positive denominators](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/efa7e31daea939d483f0897b939a9b07016ed216ec2df7ae7bcc9e56dcf2962a.svg)

*The same measured image objects are re-evaluated at p95, p99 and p99.5 blank-score cutoffs. The paired panel retains the p99 dual-positive numerator and denominator. Alternative cutoffs are sensitivity settings, not biological repeats or confidence levels. The blank supplies the thresholds, so its own positive fraction is not an independent false-positive estimate.*

The [individual composite pages](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156) show field 01 for every condition, selected by field number rather than brightness, with links to the blank. All available fields contribute to the table; Or85b has only one, and the other tuning conditions have two. No statistical comparison of independent cultures is inferred from these technical fields. The image source folders were corrected on 13 October and all analysis outputs rerun with unchanged algorithms; the records here use the corrected condition assignments.

### Base fluorescence difference R

Calculated from archived paired baselines and peak three-point means. Each cell is one well; no uncertainty interval or significance test is inferred.

| Addition | Or7a | Or19a | Or42a | Or98a | Or22a | Or67a | Or67b | Or59b | Or85b | Or35a | Orco only | Untransfected |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| VUAA1 | -0.0549 | +0.0227 | -0.0263 | -0.0198 | +0.0485 | -0.0010 | +0.0002 | -0.0370 | +0.0243 | +0.1373 | +0.2148 | +0.0041 |
| 3-octanol | +0.0961 | +0.0095 | -0.0051 | +0.0103 | -0.0094 | +0.0294 | +0.0188 | +0.0257 | +0.0212 | +0.0130 | +0.0730 | +0.0275 |
| benzaldehyde | +0.1201 | +0.0265 | +0.0677 | +0.0368 | +0.0360 | -0.0135 | +0.0398 | +0.0478 | +0.0227 | +0.0453 | +0.1378 | +0.0744 |
| 2-heptanone | +0.1835 | +0.0360 | +0.0569 | +0.0169 | +0.0320 | +0.0330 | +0.0382 | +0.0355 | -0.0063 | +0.0648 | +0.1855 | +0.0416 |
| valeric acid | -0.0276 | +0.0116 | -0.0061 | +0.0022 | -0.0170 | +0.0103 | +0.0002 | +0.0026 | +0.2167 | +0.2946 | +0.1577 | -0.0104 |
| buffer only | -0.0307 | +0.0561 | +0.3150 | -0.0159 | +0.1267 | -0.1341 | -0.0853 | +0.0649 | +0.0600 | +0.4486 | -0.0167 | -0.0550 |


### Reading the effect of each control

The same VUAA1 stimulus provides a compact comparison of all twelve columns. Reading R, then B, then D asks three different questions: how the second round differs from the first in one well; how that value compares with the same-condition buffer-only well; and how much remains after the equivalent untransfected-cell contrast.

![VUAA1 control dependence across all twelve conditions](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/b7027a9f75f3fc351586da75f97525a23d2adbef56c52702c488e1edeb16c8ff.svg)

*VUAA1 row A, one well per condition. The plot shows the computed R→B→D progression, without adding error bars or a significance threshold. Fusion-only A11 remains positive; Or35a changes sign after its large buffer reference is subtracted; Or67a and Or67b increase after subtraction of negative buffer references. The untransfected D value is zero by construction and is a control identity, not independent evidence of no response.*

This comparison makes the control dependence explicit. A control correction can increase, decrease or reverse an observed contrast; none of those operations identifies its biological cause. The full retained stimulus table above and the condition-specific part tables should be read alongside this single-stimulus overview.

### Selected control contrasts

| Well | Condition / addition | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A11 | ORCO only / VUAA1 | +0.2148 | +0.2316 | +0.1725 |
| A10 | Or35a+ORCO / VUAA1 | +0.1373 | -0.3113 | -0.3704 |
| F01 | Or7a+ORCO / 2-heptanone | +0.1835 | +0.2141 | +0.1176 |
| F09 | Or85b+ORCO / 2-heptanone | -0.0063 | -0.0664 | -0.1629 |
| G09 | Or85b+ORCO / valeric acid | +0.2167 | +0.1567 | +0.1121 |
| H03 | Or42a+ORCO / buffer only | +0.3150 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |
| H10 | Or35a+ORCO / buffer only | +0.4486 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |


A11 remains positive after both contrasts. A10 has positive R but negative B and D because its buffer reference H10 is larger. F01 remains positive after correction, yet its R partly reflects subtraction of a declining blank round. Selecting the largest value, or treating every negative contrast as a nonfunctional receptor, would be misleading. Part pages report every retained B and D per construct; the CSV retains all 96 wells.

![Paired-round examples and control dependence](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/ed1852be52e63327b879ed6dd1ec2c5368d2e15013b9703addd35a4da7084950.avif)

*Selected traces compare first and second response runs. This is a diagnostic comparison, not classification of true or false responses. Time is relative to each exported run, not a precisely recorded addition.*

The combined record documents prepared plasmid samples, reporter-associated fluorescence in fixed cells, and exploratory changes in a later plate assay. These answer different questions. They do not together prove membrane-localized, receptor-specific detection without the missing identity, vehicle, calcium-dependence and replication controls.

entries.title: What another team can reuse and what must be validated next
entries.body_markdown:
The contribution is a modular design with traceable measurements and explicit controls. The evidence does not establish a validated sensor collection. Fourteen basic components were not tested independently; eleven composite conditions were not independently repeated. Pages and technical fields do not increase biological replication.

The consequential gaps are numeric gain, verified stimulus and vehicle preparation, experimental-plasmid identity, cell state and handling timing. Resolve these, then repeat a focused positive-control and ligand panel with independent cultures and matched controls. Assess expression, localization and calcium dependence separately. Reproducible responses should precede concentration-response modelling, specificity, stability or detection-limit claims.

R is sensitive to a first-round decrease, while B and D depend on additional wells. Neither calculation identifies the biological explanation. Complete traces, both rounds and controls are more informative than selecting the normalization producing the largest value.

### Practical reuse of the collection

| Starting point | What is supplied | What the next user needs to establish |
|---|---|---|
| One tuning CDS | Reference identifiers, submitted sequence length, assembly-site scan and matching module | Expression context and a suitable functional readout |
| OR-IRES-mCherry module | Bicistronic layout, marker-associated endpoint evidence and its condition-specific P2 values | Co-expression with the reporter fusion, localization and ligand/vehicle controls |
| Reporter–Orco fusion | Domain layout, fusion-only microscopy and VUAA1/control traces | Intact protein, calcium dependence and reproducibility in the chosen host |
| Analysis workflow | Original calculation code, methods, small characterization tables and traceable exclusions | Recorded inputs and fixed acquisition settings for any new dataset |

The collection is useful as a documented starting architecture and a worked example of control-sensitive fluorescence analysis. It is not yet a completed, validated multi-odor sensor. The part pages preserve the differences among conditions rather than treating the presence of 25 sequences as 25 successful functional tests.

### Reproducible team evidence

Analysis code and reusable documentation are published in the official iGEM GitLab repository. The three small derived characterization tables below accompany the documentation; they preserve the canonical values and quality flags. Original RFU exports, complete time-series data and microscopy TIFFs remain in the unpublished Zenodo preparation package. No Zenodo DOI or public raw-data download is claimed.

- [P2 well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/257ea425bbdd-plate-p2-well-summary.csv): both round-level changes and all-well flags.
- [P2 control contrasts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/df638ed341f7-plate-p2-control-contrasts.csv): R, B, D and their reference wells, including excluded rows clearly flagged.
- [Microscopy condition counts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/0adc745db174-nuclear-object-per-condition.csv): field counts, denominators and all three threshold settings.
- [Executed P2 methods](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/b826bffef90c-plate-p2-methods.pdf) and [P2 analysis code](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/final-test/analyze_plate_p2.py).
- [Microscopy analysis code](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/microscopy/analyze_nuclear_objects.py).

entries.title: Test 2 odor assay layout and within-stage drift correction
entries.body_markdown: ### What was measured Test 2 contains **72 observed wells**: six stimulus rows × twelve construct positions. Its archive key is `odor-2026-10-21`; the source exports record 21 October 2026 with no timezone. It is distinct from Test 1, the four-acquisition assay, and its column order must not be transferred from that assay. Rows B/C were not supplied here; they are not gain-based exclusions from this dataset. ![Odor panel: construct mapping and recorded acquisition windows](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/3539a705f9f880fdad4b41ae2d8323c585a7eeb27b7dd26d218b5cf3809f08bc.avif) *An experimental schematic based on the supplied map and exported sampling times. It describes the observed assay layout and calculation, not a measured molecular mechanism.* | Row | Addition | Supplied preparation | |---|---|---| | A | VUAA1 | 1:100 dilution | | D | Isopentyl acetate | 1:1,000 dilution | | E | 2-Heptanone | 1:1,000 dilution | | F | Valeric acid | 1:1,000 dilution | | G | Pentyl acetate | 1:1,000 dilution | | H | DMSO vehicle | 0.1% DMSO | The user reports 0.1% DMSO for the solutions. These preparation facts are retained as supplied; absolute molar concentrations cannot be inferred from dilution factors alone. The older assay's nominal VUAA1 concentration is not reused here. | Column | Condition | Corresponding composite | |---|---|---| | 1 | Or7a+ORCO | [BBa_26ZAGFK0](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26zagfk0#odor-2026-10-21) | | 2 | Or19a+ORCO | [BBa_2629NIWH](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-2629niwh#odor-2026-10-21) | | 3 | Or22a+ORCO | [BBa_26WOX4B1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26wox4b1#odor-2026-10-21) | | 4 | Or35a+ORCO | [BBa_26LLF3LM](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26llf3lm#odor-2026-10-21) | | 5 | Or42a+ORCO | [BBa_26Q1Q094](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q1q094#odor-2026-10-21) | | 6 | Or59b+ORCO | [BBa_26Y7CI2H](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26y7ci2h#odor-2026-10-21) | | 7 | Or67a+ORCO | [BBa_265G8CE1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265g8ce1#odor-2026-10-21) | | 8 | Or67b+ORCO | [BBa_269VSDDR](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-269vsddr#odor-2026-10-21) | | 9 | Or85b+ORCO | [BBa_26K1TU11](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26k1tu11#odor-2026-10-21) | | 10 | Or98a+ORCO | [BBa_26TZLBMJ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26tzlbmj#odor-2026-10-21) | | 11 | ORCO only | [BBa_26E11Z80](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) | | 12 | No transfection | Cellular background control; no part assigned | ### Primary calculation: change within F1 minus change within F0 For each well, use the first and last actual reading in each acquisition: - **ΔF0 = 100 × [F0(48 s) / F0(0 s) − 1]**, in percent. - **ΔF1 = 100 × [F1(168 s) / F1(0 s) − 1]**, in percent. - **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). F0 has five readings at 12 s intervals and F1 has fifteen. This subtracts the observed baseline-stage disturbance from the observed within-F1 fluorescence change. It uses separate denominators for the two stages. No baseline line is extrapolated to 168 s, and no rate, peak value or mean F1/F0 ratio is substituted for these endpoints. The primary S windows are unequal: **48 s of F0 versus 168 s of F1**. Therefore the data also include **S48 = 100 × [F1(48 s)/F1(0 s) − 1] − ΔF0**, using equal 48 s windows. S48 is a sensitivity view of the recorded data, not an independent replicate or evidence that the longer-duration result is incorrect. The separate vehicle contrast is **S(stimulus,c) − S(H,c)**. A further no-transfection contrast subtracts the corresponding vehicle contrast in column 12. These are differences between individual wells, with shared references; they remain dependent descriptive comparisons. Vehicle subtraction is additional to the primary within-well drift subtraction. ### Relation to Test 1 Test 1 had four acquisitions: a baseline before the blank addition, the blank round, a baseline before the test addition and the test round. Its retained calculation uses peak-three fluorescence changes and subtracts the blank-round excursion. Test 2 has only F0 and F1. **S is not the Test 1 R metric**, and these results are not pooled as replicated measurements of a single statistic. The Test 1 values remain unchanged and separately defined in their original tables. The mean-ratio metric **100 × (mean F1 / mean F0 − 1)** remains in the [mean-ratio audit](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv). It describes a different question and no longer supplies the main response conclusion. An F1 trajectory can rise even if its entire acquisition lies below the earlier F0 acquisition. Source timestamps do not identify the injection time, so no continuous injection-aligned trace is inferred. ### Reproducible inputs and limits There is one observed well per condition–addition pair. Five baseline readings and fifteen subsequent readings are within-well sampling, not twenty biological replicates. Numeric acquisition settings, stock molarities, addition-to-read delay and clone/culture lineage are not independently established from these exports. Within-stage normalization avoids making the between-acquisition level offset the response metric; it does not establish the biological cause of the trajectory. Local attachments: [corrected summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [mean-ratio audit](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv), [analysis metadata](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/05775ad28370-change-summary.json) and [import manifest](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json). Original measurements remain under `zenodo-release/aerosense-wiki/data/odor-2026-10-21/raw/`. New files have not been assigned an invented public DOI or Registry URL.

entries.title: Using the drift-adjusted profiles for the next experiment
entries.body_markdown:
The additional dataset contributes inspectable within-stage trajectories, a baseline-drift correction, explicitly supplied vehicle preparation and a complete construct map. The rising VUAA1 trajectories are represented by the corrected S statistic; their lower between-acquisition mean levels are retained as a different descriptive audit. Neither comparison should be used to erase the other or to infer an unrecorded injection transient.

Positive S is consistent with a fluorescence increase during F1 that exceeds the measured F0-stage drift. It does not isolate receptor-dependent calcium entry from other time-dependent cellular, chemical or optical effects. The unequal time windows, separate vehicle wells and absence of independent cultures limit causal interpretation. Inspect S48 and the entire traces before choosing the repeat experiment; repeat the relevant stimulus, vehicle, ORCO-only and no-transfection controls under documented fixed settings and timings.

The Test 1 four-acquisition metric and Test 2 two-acquisition metric stay distinct. The receptor coding sequences and individual fusion domains retain Design-only status, because all these measurements concern assembled expression conditions. Sequence confirmation, protein localization, dose dependence, selectivity and detection limits remain separate validation questions.

entries.title: Or19a expression module with an independent fluorescent marker
entries.body_markdown:
This module is intended to supply the tuning receptor in a co-expression system with GCaMP6f–Orco (`BBa_26E11Z80`). The receptor and co-receptor form the expected sensing complex; the IRES drives translation of mCherry as a separate protein. Red fluorescence is an expression-associated marker, not a measurement of receptor abundance, surface localization or channel function.

The receptor's design source is recorded on its CDS page. Team records describe human codon adaptation and GenScript synthesis in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Neither enhanced expression from codon adaptation nor an optimal OR:Orco ratio has been established by a matched comparison.

### Functional architecture

![Or19a bicistronic architecture](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/a4223e89242839ba37a383f115050e5883f214727dfee3b9df1688758c67076a.svg)

*Design schematic, not to scale: the Or19a coding sequence is followed by EMCV IRES and mCherry. Or19a and mCherry are separate proteins; the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion is supplied by a separate co-expressed construct. Membrane localization and channel function are hypotheses to test, not observations established by the diagram.*

### Literature context

The stable-cell study of Zboray et al. included Or19a but did not obtain responses to its tested VOC panel. That result motivates checking the expression system and ligand selection separately.

The [collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156) records the tested ligand panel and its selection limits. This screen is not an exhaustive ligand profile for this receptor.

entries.title: Or19a condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or19a+ORCO, with **242 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **25/242 (10.3%)**, GREEN-positive **1/242 (0.4%)**, and both-positive **0/242 (0.0%)**. Eligible objects represented 16.2% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or19a+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/7643929086f73b37659ef672bf1e08d2a8e5a702bae1a992e94916830a1ec471.avif)

*Or19a+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 49/242 (20.2%) | 7/242 (2.9%) |
| p99 | 25/242 (10.3%) | 1/242 (0.4%) |
| p99.5 | 25/242 (10.3%) | 1/242 (0.4%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

Twenty-five RED-positive objects remain at both p99 and p99.5, whereas only one GREEN-positive object remains and none is dual-positive at p99. Thus the separate expression marker is the clearest endpoint observation; these fields do not establish robust co-expression of both modules.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). entries.title: Interpretation and next validation for the Or19a condition
entries.body_markdown:
Every retained stimulus has a small positive R, yet every B and D is negative. The change follows directly from H02: the buffer-only well has R = **+0.0561**, larger than the retained stimulus R values. For VUAA1, the successive values are R = **+0.0227**, B = **−0.0334**, and D = **−0.0924**. Showing all three prevents a small between-round increase from being described as a receptor response.

Endpoint imaging detects the independent red marker in 25/242 eligible objects but only one GREEN-positive object and no dual-positive objects at p99. This makes expression and co-expression an immediate interpretive question, although it cannot explain the P2 outcome without a batch link. The data support testing expression-associated signal and a defined ligand panel separately; they do not establish Or19a inactivity or sensitivity.

The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **2,468 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×1; BsaI×1; BsmBI×1; BbsI×3**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Sources and references

- Reproducible methods: [nuclear-object analysis](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/microscopy/analyze_nuclear_objects.py) and [executed P2 methods](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/b826bffef90c-plate-p2-methods.pdf).

The collection distinguishes these small derived attachments from the unpublished raw-data archive.

entries.title: Or19a: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or19a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 2**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or19a: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/0be83e89-d65a-4d12-8d16-ed29c4a90798/3c206318c2433be06063af6cad8af1c1b4f65b7d45367958a1a8b56b9cbf580e.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/acaf51551928957a2b411c9798552fe592e55e722cee6e8c44a6dd13041a40a2.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A02 | VUAA1 | -2.27 | +6.67 | +8.94 | +9.43 | +6.13 | | D02 | Isopentyl acetate | -2.52 | -2.54 | -0.01 | +0.48 | +1.26 | | E02 | 2-Heptanone | -2.41 | -2.27 | +0.14 | +0.63 | +0.95 | | F02 | Valeric acid | -2.80 | -1.81 | +0.99 | +1.48 | +1.64 | | G02 | Pentyl acetate | -2.04 | -2.27 | -0.23 | +0.26 | +0.90 | | H02 | DMSO vehicle | -2.66 | -3.15 | -0.49 | +0.00 | +1.39 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +8.94 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -0.49 pp**. Their difference is **+9.43 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+6.67%**, while F0 changes **-2.27%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +8.94 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -0.49 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+9.43 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +6.13 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+9.43 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.

entries.title: An N-terminal detection handle for the reporter fusion
entries.body_markdown:
The published sequence is **105 bp**, encoding a 35-amino-acid N-terminal leader derived from the pRSET vector series. It includes a His-tag/Xpress-associated detection region and is placed before GCaMP6f in `BBa_26E11Z80`. The pRSET manual describes the parent vector's 6×His tag, T7 gene-10 leader, Xpress epitope and enterokinase site [1]; the actual assembled sequence should determine which residues and cleavage context are present.

### Intended use

The leader offers an antibody-based route to assess protein abundance and apparent molecular size, independently of calcium-dependent GCaMP brightness. A Western blot could help establish whether a full-length product is detectable. It would not, by itself, establish membrane localization or channel activity; these require other measurements.

The sequence is a synthetic vector-derived element. Its N-terminal position does not prove that it is biologically inert or incapable of affecting folding. No tagged-versus-untagged comparison has been performed.

### Functional architecture

![RSET leader within the reporter fusion](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/44af0dc03c9d2dfe772bec1acfd0ae16979dd5b2d3df07a4c5044d45300a1b94.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The 105 bp RSET leader is upstream of GCaMP6f and supplies the fusion translation start; it is a detection-handle design rather than a tested purification or localization element.*

### Reading this component within the tested fusion

The parent [BBa_26E11Z80](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80) carries this leader ahead of the calcium indicator. Its construction, fixed-cell images and P2 traces describe the complete fusion. None measures anti-tag binding or cleavage, so the leader should be selected for its sequence-defined detection handle rather than an experimentally established improvement in this sensor.

For reuse, the key junction is the in-frame connection to GCaMP6f: this leader provides the upstream translation start that the submitted GCaMP6f fragment lacks. If the leader is removed, an appropriate replacement start context must be supplied. A tag-directed assay can answer whether an intact product is detected; calcium imaging answers a different question about the fluorescent reporter.

### Characterisation status

No anti-His or anti-Xpress blot, cleavage experiment or purification result is documented for this part. The parent fusion's exploratory fluorescence is not an isolated test of tag performance. Accordingly, no detection efficiency, cleavage efficiency or lack of functional interference is claimed.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **105 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **none**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Reference

1. Invitrogen / Thermo Fisher Scientific. *pRSET A, B, and C user manual*. https://tools.thermofisher.com/content/sfs/manuals/prset_man.pdf



### Additional parent-system characterization

The [parent reporter–Orco fusion](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) includes the complete Test 2 ORCO-only profile, using within-F1 change minus within-F0 drift. Its [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) distinguish this calculation from Test 1 and retain the equal-duration sensitivity result. The ORCO-only label refers to the assembled fusion-system condition; it does not establish an independent measurement of the isolated RSET leader or compare alternative component designs.

entries.title: Or67a expression module with an independent fluorescent marker
entries.body_markdown:
This module is intended to supply the tuning receptor in a co-expression system with GCaMP6f–Orco (`BBa_26E11Z80`). The receptor and co-receptor form the expected sensing complex; the IRES drives translation of mCherry as a separate protein. Red fluorescence is an expression-associated marker, not a measurement of receptor abundance, surface localization or channel function.

The receptor's design source is recorded on its CDS page. Team records describe human codon adaptation and GenScript synthesis in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Neither enhanced expression from codon adaptation nor an optimal OR:Orco ratio has been established by a matched comparison.

### Functional architecture

![Or67a bicistronic architecture](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/1bd9bea89897e7d3755fe6f46fe7b2b4022f9b9e7c2463be2f7443a0f9519ce6.svg)

*Design schematic, not to scale: the Or67a coding sequence is followed by EMCV IRES and mCherry. Or67a and mCherry are separate proteins; the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion is supplied by a separate co-expressed construct. Membrane localization and channel function are hypotheses to test, not observations established by the diagram.*

### Literature context

The DoOR 2.0 resource provides primary experimental provenance for Drosophila odor-response profiles. Its measurements span biological contexts and normalization methods; they should guide ligand selection rather than be treated as quantitative predictions for this HEK293 calcium assay.

The [collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156) records the tested ligand panel and its selection limits. This screen is not an exhaustive ligand profile for this receptor.

### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or67a+ORCO, with **161 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **17/161 (10.6%)**, GREEN-positive **6/161 (3.7%)**, and both-positive **4/161 (2.5%)**. Eligible objects represented 10.6% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

Six GREEN-positive objects remain at both p99 and p99.5, while the RED count changes from 17 to 16. Four objects are dual-positive at p99. This supports localized co-detection in a subset of eligible objects, but does not measure the OR:Orco protein ratio or receptor localization.

entries.body_markdown:
The same-condition buffer H06 has R = **−0.1341**, so subtracting it shifts every retained stimulus upward. In A06 the near-zero VUAA1 result R = **−0.0010** becomes B = **+0.1331** and D = **+0.0740**. This is a positive contrast generated in part by the depressed reference; it is not evidence that the test trace itself rose by 13.31%.

For benzaldehyde E06, B = +0.1206 becomes D = −0.0089 after the untransfected adjustment. The sign and magnitude must therefore be read together with the reference wells. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/a56c0b48f833f4160997f625e47ede296153728aee7acf480583ac4d53fb1d1f.avif). The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. entries.title: Or67b expression module with an independent fluorescent marker
entries.body_markdown:
This module is intended to supply the tuning receptor in a co-expression system with GCaMP6f–Orco (`BBa_26E11Z80`). The receptor and co-receptor form the expected sensing complex; the IRES drives translation of mCherry as a separate protein. Red fluorescence is an expression-associated marker, not a measurement of receptor abundance, surface localization or channel function.

The receptor's design source is recorded on its CDS page. Team records describe human codon adaptation and GenScript synthesis in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Neither enhanced expression from codon adaptation nor an optimal OR:Orco ratio has been established by a matched comparison.

### Functional architecture

![Or67b bicistronic architecture](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/7a96baab910b8f7ac5b2df2e2fa28f6f8f02adb7662abe6d367a5bac81481532.svg)

*Design schematic, not to scale: the Or67b coding sequence is followed by EMCV IRES and mCherry. Or67b and mCherry are separate proteins; the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion is supplied by a separate co-expressed construct. Membrane localization and channel function are hypotheses to test, not observations established by the diagram.*

### Literature context

Zboray et al. included Or67b among the receptors examined, but it was not among their seven functionally profiled lines. This is not evidence that Or67b lacks biological function.

The [collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156) records the tested ligand panel and its selection limits. This screen is not an exhaustive ligand profile for this receptor.

entries.title: Or67b condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or67b+ORCO, with **193 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **14/193 (7.3%)**, GREEN-positive **2/193 (1.0%)**, and both-positive **2/193 (1.0%)**. Eligible objects represented 9.5% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or67b+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/38ddc265d08ba416e3c4c3c2638a89cb21ddd9dc74b66f69f115297849e4bae3.avif)

*Or67b+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 46/193 (23.8%) | 11/193 (5.7%) |
| p99 | 14/193 (7.3%) | 2/193 (1.0%) |
| p99.5 | 13/193 (6.7%) | 2/193 (1.0%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

The two GREEN-positive objects remain at both p99 and p99.5 and are both dual-positive at p99. The RED count changes from 14 to 13. These are endpoint expression-associated observations in two technical fields, not an independent functional test of the receptor.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A07 | VUAA1 | -0.0035 | -0.0034 | +0.0002 | +0.0854 | +0.0264 |
| D07 | 3-octanol | +0.0149 | +0.0337 | +0.0188 | +0.1040 | +0.0215 |
| E07 | benzaldehyde | +0.0016 | +0.0414 | +0.0398 | +0.1250 | -0.0044 |
| F07 | 2-heptanone | -0.0043 | +0.0339 | +0.0382 | +0.1235 | +0.0269 |
| G07 | valeric acid | +0.0279 | +0.0282 | +0.0002 | +0.0855 | +0.0409 |
| H07 | buffer only | -0.0199 | -0.1052 | -0.0853 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

B and D for the buffer row are zero by construction. Rows B (ethyl propionate) and C (isopentyl acetate) are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes; their raw data remain in the archive. Nominal VUAA1 final concentration is 50 µM in the source report, not independently verified. Final VOC molarity, numeric detector gain and matched DMSO vehicle concentration remain unresolved.

![Or67b: two sequential measurement rounds](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/15e4e87dd2b9f5111610148ad6f45dd9ae53cd8610c1ea470f45c46ff8a40d1c.avif)

*Test 1 paired-round plot: plain assay buffer in round 1, test addition in round 2, each normalized to its own baseline. These are two stages of Test 1, not Test 1 versus Test 2. Plain buffer is not a documented DMSO-matched vehicle. The plot shows both individual rounds; the table supplies R and the between-well B and D contrasts.*

entries.title: An N-terminal calcium indicator tethered to the olfactory co-receptor
entries.body_markdown:
The fusion is intended to report calcium changes in an Orco-containing sensing system. Insect odorant receptors have an intracellular N-terminus in the established topology [1], which motivates placing GCaMP6f on that side. A single ORF encodes one copy of each domain, but this does not guarantee intact mature protein, equal functional stoichiometry or plasma-membrane localization.

The related stable-cell architecture of Zboray et al. provides a design precedent [2]. Our linker is (GGGGS)₃, 15 amino acids, compared with their eight-amino-acid connector. Its intended flexibility is a design rationale; no side-by-side linker comparison establishes an advantage. The different host-expression arrangements and acquisition methods also prevent assigning differences between the two studies to linker length.

### Functional architecture

![Reporter–co-receptor fusion architecture](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/ef416bf396dd17c80f5cf652ae9bcd21d5a3c0956e4624fdb0157c4a4a6296b6.svg)

*Design schematic, not to scale. The RSET leader, GCaMP6f, (GGGGS)₃ linker and DmOrco form one open reading frame. The intended intracellular reporter placement follows the established Orco topology; the diagram does not establish the localization, integrity or channel function of this construct in our cells.*

| Component | Part | Design source |
|---|---|---|
| RSET leader | BBa_262WP16P | pRSET vector-derived detection handle |
| GCaMP6f | BBa_26QHYP02 | Chen et al.; team record cites Addgene #40755 |
| (GGGGS)₃ linker | BBa_26E21OEQ | Synthetic glycine–serine connector |
| DmOrco | BBa_26LWIKBQ | FlyBase FBgn0037324 / FBtr0078794; RefSeq NP_524235 |

Team records describe GenScript synthesis in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Component pages document the sequence origins and reuse constraints. Neither the leader's neutrality nor the localization of this complete fusion has been directly established.

entries.title: Fusion-only condition: microscopy and VUAA1-associated fluorescence
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The image condition labelled “ORCO only” contains this reporter fusion without a tuning-receptor module. Across **three technical fields**, **342 eligible DAPI objects** were retained. At the blank-derived p99 threshold, **24/342 (7.0%)** were GREEN-positive, **0/342 (0.0%)** were RED-positive, and none were positive in both channels. Eligible objects represented **19.6%** of DAPI foreground. The absence of an mCherry module makes the red channel a useful control within this image set.

These fixed-cell measurements are localized reporter-associated fluorescence counts, not a whole-culture transfection efficiency or evidence of membrane localization. The blank yielded 1/170 objects above each threshold but also supplied the cutoff, so it is not an independent false-positive-rate estimate. The microscopy batch cannot currently be linked to P2 at plasmid-batch or culture level.

The first numbered fusion-only field is shown below. The GREEN channel tests for reporter-associated signal, while the RED channel provides a particularly useful check because this condition lacks an mCherry expression module.

![ORCO-only field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/543a1b4d8437db952db547a6ce0c929a9a22fa47c4a0fef61f6e6f7bc0f64d35.avif)

*Fusion-only field 01; brightfield retains exported levels and BLUE/GREEN/RED display windows are 0–255/0–120/0–180. The original 100 µm scale bars remain visible. Quantification uses original TIFF intensities, not these display panels. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp).*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 47/342 (13.7%) | 50/342 (14.6%) |
| p99 | 0/342 (0.0%) | 24/342 (7.0%) |
| p99.5 | 0/342 (0.0%) | 19/342 (5.6%) |

*All three fusion-only fields; the same 342 eligible objects are evaluated at each alternative blank-score cutoff. These cutoffs are sensitivity settings, not statistical confidence levels.*

At p95, 47 objects exceed the RED criterion despite the absence of mCherry; at p99 and p99.5, none does. This is a useful internal warning against equating permissive threshold crossings with expression. GREEN-positive objects remain at both stricter cutoffs (24 and 19), supporting localized reporter-associated fluorescence. The image does not identify its subcellular location or establish a functional channel.

### Test 1: exploratory paired-round assay

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

The raw headers span **10–11 October 2026**. There is one well per condition–stimulus combination and no documented independent biological repetition. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well, and D also subtracts the corresponding untransfected contrast. Equations and source files are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A11 | VUAA1 | -0.0962 | +0.1186 | +0.2148 | +0.2316 | +0.1725 |
| D11 | 3-octanol | +0.0475 | +0.1205 | +0.0730 | +0.0897 | +0.0072 |
| E11 | benzaldehyde | +0.0267 | +0.1645 | +0.1378 | +0.1545 | +0.0251 |
| F11 | 2-heptanone | +0.0248 | +0.2103 | +0.1855 | +0.2022 | +0.1056 |
| G11 | valeric acid | +0.0395 | +0.1972 | +0.1577 | +0.1744 | +0.1298 |
| H11 | buffer only | +0.0132 | -0.0035 | -0.0167 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

Rows B and C are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes. VUAA1 is nominally 50 µM final according to the source report; the actual dose, final DMSO fraction and numeric gain remain unverified. Final VOC molarity is unknown. Buffer-row B and D values are zero by definition.

![Fusion-only paired-round fluorescence](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/f102157ae572590c994e38b6dc4f99855f8e4bff0c8d4dfff83f73a99da7844b.avif)

*Two sequential measurement rounds, each normalized to its own baseline. Plain assay buffer precedes the test addition. It is not a documented DMSO-matched vehicle. R is the difference of the peak three-point means; B and D additionally compare different wells.*

### What the VUAA1 well shows

A11 has ΔFblank = **−0.0962**, ΔFtest = **+0.1186**, R = **+0.2148**, B = **+0.2316** and D = **+0.1725**. Its reference wells are H11 (fusion-only buffer), A12 (VUAA1 in untransfected cells) and H12 (untransfected buffer). The positive R partly reflects subtraction of the decline during the first round; it must not be described as a 21.5% ligand-only rise.

![A11 and A12, four separate acquisition stages](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/17027c8a4ffc0865f62920df62bac5408e78d992edefaba10ebeb32a9dfc01a5.avif)

*Raw fluorescence for the fusion-only and untransfected VUAA1 wells. Each panel uses time within that exported run; gaps during manual handling are not reconstructed. The fusion-only test trace rises from 2,227 to 2,469 RFU, toward its earlier baseline level. This temporal association is observable, but does not identify the cause by itself.*

![Untransfected paired-round fluorescence](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/e9563023cc1f98a42938de94168d9d8c956251cd481642f2d3547a6d283a889e.avif)

*Untransfected cells provide biological background controls, not cell-free optical controls. Their shared use in D introduces dependence among contrasts. No noise-floor, significance or limit-of-detection claim is inferred from these single wells.*

entries.title: What the fusion-only fluorescence and its controls establish
entries.body_markdown:
The A11 observation is consistent with a response worth testing further, but this experiment alone does not prove channel gating, extracellular-calcium dependence or plasma-membrane localization. VUAA1 activation of Orco is established in the literature [3]; that prior result supports the experimental hypothesis rather than substituting for controls on this fusion.

The Orco-only condition also shows positive D values for retained odorant rows, including **+0.1056 for 2-heptanone** and **+0.1298 for valeric acid**. Thus, a positive contrast in a tuning-receptor condition cannot automatically be assigned to that receptor. The 12-second sampling and unrecorded addition-to-read delays cannot distinguish all rapid optical, mechanical and biological explanations from curve shape alone. The peak time is an acquisition statistic, not a measured channel response time.

Comparison with a selected stable-cell line cannot identify the cause of a smaller or larger amplitude here: expression context, cell handling, stimulation and normalization differ. No stable clone, optimized linker, receptor specificity, calcium affinity or detection limit has been established for this construct.

The next informative evidence would combine verified plasmid identity and expression with fixed-gain repeated cultures, concentration-matched vehicle controls, Ca²⁺-dependence controls and an appropriate localization assay. Record seeding, cell state and addition timing so that a change in fluorescence can be separated from variation in the preparation. A protein blot addresses abundance and integrity; it does not replace localization or functional controls.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **2,862 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **EcoRI×1; PstI×4; BsaI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Reproducible analysis

The [nuclear-object analysis](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/microscopy/analyze_nuclear_objects.py) documents the segmentation and blank-derived thresholds. The [executed P2 methods](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/b826bffef90c-plate-p2-methods.pdf) define each round, R, B and D. The [microscopy counts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/0adc745db174-nuclear-object-per-condition.csv), [P2 well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/257ea425bbdd-plate-p2-well-summary.csv) and [control contrasts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/df638ed341f7-plate-p2-control-contrasts.csv) accompany the documentation. The collection provides the complete condition tables and archive boundaries.

### References

1. Benton R, Sachse S, Michnick SW, Vosshall LB. Atypical membrane topology and heteromeric function of Drosophila odorant receptors in vivo. *PLoS Biology* 4(2), e20 (2006). https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.0040020
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
3. Jones PL, Pask GM, Rinker DC, Zwiebel LJ. Functional agonism of insect odorant receptor ion channels. *PNAS* 108, 8821–8825 (2011). https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1102425108
4. Chen T-W, Wardill TJ, Sun Y, et al. Ultrasensitive fluorescent proteins for imaging neuronal activity. *Nature* 499, 295–300 (2013). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature12354

entries.title: ORCO only: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the reporter-fusion system without a tuning receptor** across six additions, mapped to **column 11**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![ORCO only: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/d8902fb8-605b-4d16-b728-e6a8c0834598/ca5547f9423b0ac524b4819dcb8c55ccd30146e86ae33019699add5a35687c2b.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/031cb16bbeb716366ccf1a90fa2468499599cd55dfc0bc9291e7d0993578c8d9.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A11 | VUAA1 | -1.13 | +17.56 | +18.69 | +19.61 | +8.85 | | D11 | Isopentyl acetate | -1.08 | -3.14 | -2.06 | -1.14 | -0.20 | | E11 | 2-Heptanone | -1.21 | -1.80 | -0.59 | +0.33 | +0.58 | | F11 | Valeric acid | -1.02 | -1.58 | -0.56 | +0.36 | +0.17 | | G11 | Pentyl acetate | -1.35 | -2.02 | -0.66 | +0.25 | +0.64 | | H11 | DMSO vehicle | -1.23 | -2.15 | -0.92 | +0.00 | +0.37 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +18.69 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -0.92 pp**. Their difference is **+19.61 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the table below and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+17.56%**, while F0 changes **-1.13%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +18.69 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -0.92 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+19.61 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +8.85 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+19.61 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. This row remains a reporter-fusion control; it is not a tuning-receptor ligand profile. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.
