entries.title: A synthetic 15-amino-acid linker for a reporter–receptor fusion
entries.body_markdown:
The published sequence is **45 bp**, encoding **(GGGGS)₃**, a 15-amino-acid glycine–serine linker. It is placed in frame between GCaMP6f and DmOrco in `BBa_26E11Z80`, without an intervening stop codon. Its purpose is to provide a flexible connection while retaining a single fusion protein.

### Design rationale

Zboray et al. used an eight-amino-acid Gly₂SerGly₃SerGly connector in their related reporter–Orco architecture [1]. The present construct uses a longer connector as a design choice intended to allow domain motion. No matched comparison establishes that 15 amino acids improves folding, expression, localization or signal over eight amino acids.

This is a synthetic sequence rather than a gene from an organism. The three peptide repeats use diversified synonymous codons. That sequence choice does not guarantee freedom from synthesis errors or instability; the assembled product should still be sequence-verified.

### Functional architecture

![Glycine–serine linker between reporter and receptor](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/872e583863427cf7823b9988793bd0013220da7f8e9395b52b607bcade80e147.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted 45 bp (GGGGS)₃ segment joins GCaMP6f to DmOrco in frame. It is an internal connector, not an independent protein or a measured improvement over another linker.*

### Junction-specific reuse

The linker makes the two domains a single translational product while allowing a flexible connection. Its two junctions, with the end of GCaMP6f and the start of DmOrco, are therefore the relevant sequence features for reuse. Preserve the reading frame and the intended domain order; changing the length, composition or attachment point creates a different fusion design.

The parent [BBa_26E11Z80](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80) documents the assembly context, fixed-cell fluorescence and P2 measurements. They provide evidence about a construct containing this linker, but no comparison isolates the linker's contribution. A useful comparative study would keep the remaining fusion and expression context constant while comparing connector variants; no result from such a comparison is claimed here.

### Characterisation status

The linker was not isolated or tested across a length series. The exploratory P2 observations belong to the complete fusion and cannot establish the linker's optimum length or functional neutrality. Reuse should preserve the reading frame and test the behavior of the complete fusion in its intended host.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **45 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **none**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Reference

1. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional parent-system characterization

The [parent reporter–Orco fusion](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) includes the complete Test 2 ORCO-only profile, using within-F1 change minus within-F0 drift. Its [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) distinguish this calculation from Test 1 and retain the equal-duration sensitivity result. The ORCO-only label refers to the assembled fusion-system condition; it does not establish an independent measurement of the isolated linker or compare alternative component designs.

entries.title: Or35a coding sequence for assembly into an olfactory receptor expression system
entries.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or35a subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or35a CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/8d74a99ca32a4b1638861e91f2aa49ca1befbe810331c315cd27a9a385e1e145.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or35a CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0028946](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0028946.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0080781 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_723916](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_723916) |
| Reference protein length | 409 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_26LLF3LM module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26llf3lm) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or35a-labelled colony plate (photograph 1, lower-right), gel B lanes 1–2, the fixed-cell **Or35a+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 10**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,230 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×1; BsaI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or35a+ORCO to column 4**. The corresponding [BBa_26LLF3LM module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26llf3lm#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within-F1 changes after subtraction of F0-stage drift. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) define the two time windows, percentage-point units and equal-duration sensitivity calculation.

These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.

![Or19a CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/fd472a3f3b40917616790633fd1080cd6f128c9430f5ed5ebaa2d872cd695070.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or19a CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0041626](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0041626.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0070029 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_525013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_525013) |
| Reference protein length | 387 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_2629NIWH module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-2629niwh) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or19a-labelled colony plate (photograph 2, upper-right), gel D lanes 5–6, the fixed-cell **Or19a+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 02**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,164 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **BsaI×1; BsmBI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or19a+ORCO to column 2**. The corresponding [BBa_2629NIWH module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-2629niwh#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within-F1 changes after subtraction of F0-stage drift. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) define the two time windows, percentage-point units and equal-duration sensitivity calculation.

These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.

entries.title: Or85b condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **1 technical fields** labelled Or85b+ORCO, with **156 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **25/156 (16.0%)**, GREEN-positive **8/156 (5.1%)**, and both-positive **7/156 (4.5%)**. Eligible objects represented 18.9% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or85b+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/e6d56c8fe0fceb2b49a6059ed52b4dc1c9933c9d805279643e26cd31707ac238.avif)

*Or85b+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 48/156 (30.8%) | 14/156 (9.0%) |
| p99 | 25/156 (16.0%) | 8/156 (5.1%) |
| p99.5 | 24/156 (15.4%) | 7/156 (4.5%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

Only one field was available, so the denominator of 156 objects describes that field rather than between-field reproducibility. Twenty-four RED-positive and seven GREEN-positive objects remain at p99.5; seven objects are dual-positive at p99. Additional fields and independent cultures are needed before estimating a culture-level fraction.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A09 | VUAA1 | -0.0179 | +0.0065 | +0.0243 | -0.0357 | -0.0947 |
| D09 | 3-octanol | +0.0045 | +0.0257 | +0.0212 | -0.0388 | -0.1213 |
| E09 | benzaldehyde | +0.0158 | +0.0385 | +0.0227 | -0.0373 | -0.1667 |
| F09 | 2-heptanone | +0.0571 | +0.0508 | -0.0063 | -0.0664 | -0.1629 |
| G09 | valeric acid | -0.0127 | +0.2040 | +0.2167 | +0.1567 | +0.1121 |
| H09 | buffer only | -0.0602 | -0.0002 | +0.0600 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

B and D for the buffer row are zero by construction. Rows B (ethyl propionate) and C (isopentyl acetate) are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes; their raw data remain in the archive. Nominal VUAA1 final concentration is 50 µM in the source report, not independently verified. Final VOC molarity, numeric detector gain and matched DMSO vehicle concentration remain unresolved.

![Or85b: two sequential measurement rounds](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/75f8d139eae38b346860f7b1c57a1e604a1dea08d878ec624e8475bb5aacff05.avif)

*Test 1 paired-round plot: plain assay buffer in round 1, test addition in round 2, each normalized to its own baseline. These are two stages of Test 1, not Test 1 versus Test 2. Plain buffer is not a documented DMSO-matched vehicle. The plot shows both individual rounds; the table supplies R and the between-well B and D contrasts.*

entries.title: Interpretation and next validation for the Or85b condition
entries.body_markdown:
This module has a particularly relevant literature comparison: Zboray et al. used 2-heptanone as an Or85b reference ligand. In our F09 well, both individual rounds rise, but the second rises less: ΔFblank = **+0.0571**, ΔFtest = **+0.0508**, R = **−0.0063**, B = **−0.0664**, and D = **−0.1629**. P2 therefore does not reproduce a positive control-adjusted observation for this ligand under its recorded conditions. Unknown final VOC concentration and lack of independent repeats prevent a receptor-level negative conclusion.

Valeric acid G09 instead has R = **+0.2167**, B = **+0.1567**, and D = **+0.1121**. The fusion-only valeric-acid well also has positive D = +0.1298, so this observation is not evidence of Or85b specificity. The single endpoint field contains seven dual-positive objects at p99; it supports localized co-detection but cannot estimate between-field reproducibility.

The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **2,477 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×3; BbsI×5**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Sources and references

- Reproducible methods: [nuclear-object analysis](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/microscopy/analyze_nuclear_objects.py) and [executed P2 methods](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/b826bffef90c-plate-p2-methods.pdf).
- Characterization tables: [microscopy condition counts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/0adc745db174-nuclear-object-per-condition.csv), [P2 well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/257ea425bbdd-plate-p2-well-summary.csv) and [P2 control contrasts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/df638ed341f7-plate-p2-control-contrasts.csv). The collection distinguishes these small derived attachments from the unpublished raw-data archive.
- Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
- Münch D, Galizia CG. DoOR 2.0—Comprehensive Mapping of Drosophila melanogaster Odorant Responses. *Scientific Reports* 6, 21841 (2016). https://doi.org/10.1038/srep21841

entries.title: Or85b: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or85b+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 9**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or85b: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/ad5e54bd-6c31-45b5-9bf9-fcbd402a176d/879a4a4521492621ac05ba05cef706dbbe1ce6953be85af47b051786f9b3474a.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/4928f6a12980c5ec820311cb6d677d74d08fda13c67a1d7d6e14dfa4a1ce8062.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A09 | VUAA1 | -1.08 | +16.44 | +17.52 | +18.99 | +13.84 | | D09 | Isopentyl acetate | -1.19 | -2.30 | -1.11 | +0.36 | +0.52 | | E09 | 2-Heptanone | -1.21 | -1.62 | -0.41 | +1.07 | +0.66 | | F09 | Valeric acid | -1.20 | -0.91 | +0.29 | +1.77 | +0.72 | | G09 | Pentyl acetate | -1.50 | -2.45 | -0.96 | +0.52 | +0.25 | | H09 | DMSO vehicle | -1.15 | -2.62 | -1.47 | +0.00 | +0.06 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +17.52 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -1.47 pp**. Their difference is **+18.99 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+16.44%**, while F0 changes **-1.08%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +17.52 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -1.47 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+18.99 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +13.84 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+18.99 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.

![Gel B containing the paired Or35a sample lanes](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/47e61e3af7196df63c289375716b7b0377eaf0c90d32b7eec887fdb9ab72999b.avif)

*Gel B: Or35a sample lanes 1–2; a 1 kb ladder is labelled in the original panel. Lane numbering here excludes the ladder. The displayed source preserves contiguous lanes; preparation involved rigid orientation/cropping without lane splicing or intensity adjustment. The label links the image to the Or35a construction condition, not a sequence-verified isolated CDS or bicistronic clone.*

The later fixed-cell condition is labelled **Or35a+ORCO**, and P2 uses **column 10**. These labels provide the working correspondence used below. A colony-to-image-to-P2 clone/culture lineage has not been independently established. Construction images and the lane map are archived under `wetlab results/cloning/` and `assets/results/electrophoresis/`; shared extraction and handling records are in the collection.

entries.title: Or35a condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or35a+ORCO, with **200 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **28/200 (14.0%)**, GREEN-positive **11/200 (5.5%)**, and both-positive **8/200 (4.0%)**. Eligible objects represented 10.2% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or35a+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/6ffc966fa86bfd81411e389726871a464f984083a10d607260d70e7be3ad53ee.avif)

*Or35a+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 70/200 (35.0%) | 27/200 (13.5%) |
| p99 | 28/200 (14.0%) | 11/200 (5.5%) |
| p99.5 | 23/200 (11.5%) | 7/200 (3.5%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

Both channels retain positive objects at p99.5, but the counts decrease from p99: RED 28 to 23 and GREEN 11 to 7. Eight objects are dual-positive at p99. This endpoint evidence should be considered alongside the unusually large buffer-only P2 value, rather than used to resolve that later assay effect.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A10 | VUAA1 | +0.0403 | +0.1776 | +0.1373 | -0.3113 | -0.3704 |
| D10 | 3-octanol | +0.0193 | +0.0324 | +0.0130 | -0.4356 | -0.5181 |
| E10 | benzaldehyde | -0.0098 | +0.0355 | +0.0453 | -0.4033 | -0.5328 |
| F10 | 2-heptanone | -0.0402 | +0.0246 | +0.0648 | -0.3839 | -0.4804 |
| G10 | valeric acid | -0.1172 | +0.1774 | +0.2946 | -0.1540 | -0.1986 |
| H10 | buffer only | -0.0961 | +0.3525 | +0.4486 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

B and D for the buffer row are zero by construction. Rows B (ethyl propionate) and C (isopentyl acetate) are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes; their raw data remain in the archive. Nominal VUAA1 final concentration is 50 µM in the source report, not independently verified. Final VOC molarity, numeric detector gain and matched DMSO vehicle concentration remain unresolved.

![Or35a: two sequential measurement rounds](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/aeaf5085829b8bf482e4a99d2c948df12966f6a063303c9a2d7788a0304cc933.avif)

*Test 1 paired-round plot: plain assay buffer in round 1, test addition in round 2, each normalized to its own baseline. These are two stages of Test 1, not Test 1 versus Test 2. Plain buffer is not a documented DMSO-matched vehicle. The plot shows both individual rounds; the table supplies R and the between-well B and D contrasts.*

entries.title: Interpretation and next validation for the Or35a condition
entries.body_markdown:
H10 is the largest same-condition buffer reference discussed in this panel: ΔFblank = **−0.0961**, ΔFtest = **+0.3525**, and R = **+0.4486**. Even the positive VUAA1 R = **+0.1373** becomes B = **−0.3113** and D = **−0.3704**. All retained stimulus B and D values are negative because their R values are below this common reference.

The negative differences should not be called inhibitory receptor responses. They show that the buffer-only well is essential to interpretation and should be examined in a repeated preparation. The endpoint fields have eight dual-positive objects at p99, but these fixed-cell images cannot explain the unusual H10 behavior or establish a link between expression and the P2 time course.

The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **2,534 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×2; BsaI×1; BbsI×3**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Sources and references

- Reproducible methods: [nuclear-object analysis](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/microscopy/analyze_nuclear_objects.py) and [executed P2 methods](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/b826bffef90c-plate-p2-methods.pdf).
- Characterization tables: [microscopy condition counts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/0adc745db174-nuclear-object-per-condition.csv), [P2 well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/257ea425bbdd-plate-p2-well-summary.csv) and [P2 control contrasts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/df638ed341f7-plate-p2-control-contrasts.csv). The collection distinguishes these small derived attachments from the unpublished raw-data archive.
- Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
- Münch D, Galizia CG. DoOR 2.0—Comprehensive Mapping of Drosophila melanogaster Odorant Responses. *Scientific Reports* 6, 21841 (2016). https://doi.org/10.1038/srep21841
- Shaner NC, Campbell RE, Steinbach PA, et al. Improved monomeric red, orange and yellow fluorescent proteins derived from Discosoma sp. red fluorescent protein. *Nature Biotechnology* 22, 1567–1572 (2004). https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt1037

entries.title: Or35a: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or35a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 4**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or35a: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/9b13fd04-be47-493b-ac48-77c9645d9792/9e4229dd224a6e9eb43e266fd5ed608206b934c626462a85e5806c651b99a2fa.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/f713c4ba663254c55262e1d0563db68227cc4fb5ec2e55d32d0aa327dac815f4.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A04 | VUAA1 | -2.57 | +34.09 | +36.67 | +38.06 | +19.67 | | D04 | Isopentyl acetate | -2.06 | -2.68 | -0.61 | +0.78 | +0.60 | | E04 | 2-Heptanone | -3.10 | -3.04 | +0.05 | +1.44 | +1.58 | | F04 | Valeric acid | -2.72 | -0.91 | +1.81 | +3.20 | +1.14 | | G04 | Pentyl acetate | -2.17 | -3.10 | -0.93 | +0.46 | +0.75 | | H04 | DMSO vehicle | -1.60 | -2.99 | -1.39 | +0.00 | -0.11 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +36.67 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -1.39 pp**. Their difference is **+38.06 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the table below and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+34.09%**, while F0 changes **-2.57%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +36.67 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -1.39 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+38.06 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +19.67 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+38.06 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.

entries.title: The Drosophila olfactory co-receptor coding sequence
entries.body_markdown:
The published sequence is **1,461 bp**, including an ATG start and terminal stop codon, for a 486-amino-acid reference protein. Team design records identify *Drosophila melanogaster* Orco (historically Or83b), FlyBase **FBgn0037324 / FBtr0078794**, RefSeq **NP_524235**, with human codon adaptation and synthesis by GenScript.

### Biological rationale and use

Orco participates with tuning receptors in insect heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. Work in Drosophila also establishes a role in receptor localization and function [2]. These findings motivate co-expression with a tuning receptor, but they do not prove that our particular construct reaches the HEK293 plasma membrane.

VUAA1 can activate Orco-containing channels, including Orco without a tuning receptor, in published systems [3]. In this collection it is used as a functional probe, with the qualification that fluorescence changes require controls before being assigned to channel activation.

Use this bare CDS to choose your own reporter or expression arrangement. The provided composite `BBa_26E11Z80` joins GCaMP6f to the Orco N-terminus through a 15-amino-acid linker. Removing or relocating domains creates a different construct and requires a new characterization.

### Functional architecture

![DmOrco coding sequence within the shared sensing system](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/ab4b045e4a28727466318d8c3e9c61df71067e6b1e0c2183c89619b62c9adbd4.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. This basic CDS supplies the shared co-receptor sequence. In BBa_26E11Z80 its N-terminus is joined to the reporter through the linker; the ORCO-only assay label refers to that complete fusion, not this isolated CDS.*

### Which observations belong to this component

The ORCO-labelled construction plate and paired gel A lanes 1–2 are preserved on the [fusion page](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80). They establish the presence of an ORCO-labelled preparation in the workflow, but the labels do not resolve whether a standalone Orco plasmid or the fusion was photographed. They are not reassigned as sequence confirmation of this basic part.

The later fusion-only condition is useful as a control for the ten tuning-receptor modules. Its retained D values include +0.1725 for VUAA1, +0.1056 for 2-heptanone and +0.1298 for valeric acid. Thus, positive fluorescence contrasts in the collection cannot automatically be attributed to the tuning receptor. The complete fusion and its cellular background must be considered. Reusing the bare Orco CDS without GCaMP6f requires a separate readout and a fresh characterization of that arrangement.

### Characterisation status

This untagged CDS was not tested separately. The P2 column labelled “ORCO only” contains the **GCaMP6f–Orco fusion without a tuning receptor**, not this naked CDS. Its microscopy and VUAA1-associated measurements belong to the composite. They cannot be reassigned as independent functional evidence for this basic part.

Reference-protein identity is a design intention. Colony growth and undigested plasmid gels do not replace sequence confirmation of the experimental clone, and the published sequence's assembly sites should be checked before use.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,461 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×2; BsaI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Benton R, Sachse S, Michnick SW, Vosshall LB. Atypical membrane topology and heteromeric function of Drosophila odorant receptors in vivo. *PLoS Biology* 4(2), e20 (2006). https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.0040020
3. Jones PL, Pask GM, Rinker DC, Zwiebel LJ. Functional agonism of insect odorant receptor ion channels. *PNAS* 108, 8821–8825 (2011). https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1102425108



### Additional parent-system characterization

The [parent reporter–Orco fusion](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) includes the complete Test 2 ORCO-only profile, using within-F1 change minus within-F0 drift. Its [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) distinguish this calculation from Test 1 and retain the equal-duration sensitivity result. The ORCO-only label refers to the assembled fusion-system condition; it does not establish an independent measurement of untagged Orco or compare alternative component designs.

entries.title: Or59b coding sequence for assembly into an olfactory receptor expression system
entries.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or59b subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or59b CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/0e63deb27a9cbd66a9920874ceb0a16b53be4850f9f945ebeb451afe7e10b0a2.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or59b CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0034865](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0034865.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0072021 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_523822](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_523822) |
| Reference protein length | 398 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_26Y7CI2H module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26y7ci2h) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or59b-labelled colony plate (photograph 2, lower-left), gel C lanes 3–4, the fixed-cell **Or59b+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 08**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,197 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **none**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or59b+ORCO to column 6**. The corresponding [BBa_26Y7CI2H module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26y7ci2h#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within-F1 changes after subtraction of F0-stage drift. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) define the two time windows, percentage-point units and equal-duration sensitivity calculation.

These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.

entries.title: Or42a expression module with an independent fluorescent marker
entries.body_markdown:
This module is intended to supply the tuning receptor in a co-expression system with GCaMP6f–Orco (`BBa_26E11Z80`). The receptor and co-receptor form the expected sensing complex; the IRES drives translation of mCherry as a separate protein. Red fluorescence is an expression-associated marker, not a measurement of receptor abundance, surface localization or channel function.

The receptor's design source is recorded on its CDS page. Team records describe human codon adaptation and GenScript synthesis in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Neither enhanced expression from codon adaptation nor an optimal OR:Orco ratio has been established by a matched comparison.

### Functional architecture

![Or42a bicistronic architecture](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/93d522a959f13e70efbfa65a1fcd43fa5cc4e5dc5acb5384522e693f20abf0e2.svg)

*Design schematic, not to scale: the Or42a coding sequence is followed by EMCV IRES and mCherry. Or42a and mCherry are separate proteins; the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion is supplied by a separate co-expressed construct. Membrane localization and channel function are hypotheses to test, not observations established by the diagram.*

### Literature context

The DoOR 2.0 resource provides primary experimental provenance for Drosophila odor-response profiles. Its measurements span biological contexts and normalization methods; they should guide ligand selection rather than be treated as quantitative predictions for this HEK293 calcium assay.

The [collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156) records the tested ligand panel and its selection limits. This screen is not an exhaustive ligand profile for this receptor.

entries.title: Or42a condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or42a+ORCO, with **263 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **18/263 (6.8%)**, GREEN-positive **4/263 (1.5%)**, and both-positive **1/263 (0.4%)**. Eligible objects represented 22.8% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or42a+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/9b8cd373d02c8e0c7a6cff1587cd2491d2f888f5713ea963a1298b9cb958298a.avif)

*Or42a+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 88/263 (33.5%) | 19/263 (7.2%) |
| p99 | 18/263 (6.8%) | 4/263 (1.5%) |
| p99.5 | 15/263 (5.7%) | 1/263 (0.4%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

Raising the cutoff from p95 to p99 reduces the RED count from 88 to 18 and the GREEN count from 19 to 4. Only one GREEN-positive object remains at p99.5. The apparent amount of expression-associated signal therefore depends strongly on the cutoff; the image alone would overstate the number of clearly resolved positive objects.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A03 | VUAA1 | +0.0158 | -0.0105 | -0.0263 | -0.3413 | -0.4004 |
| D03 | 3-octanol | +0.0304 | +0.0253 | -0.0051 | -0.3202 | -0.4026 |
| E03 | benzaldehyde | -0.0381 | +0.0297 | +0.0677 | -0.2473 | -0.3767 |
| F03 | 2-heptanone | +0.0293 | +0.0862 | +0.0569 | -0.2581 | -0.3547 |
| G03 | valeric acid | +0.0347 | +0.0286 | -0.0061 | -0.3212 | -0.3658 |
| H03 | buffer only | -0.3008 | +0.0142 | +0.3150 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

B and D for the buffer row are zero by construction. Rows B (ethyl propionate) and C (isopentyl acetate) are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes; their raw data remain in the archive. Nominal VUAA1 final concentration is 50 µM in the source report, not independently verified. Final VOC molarity, numeric detector gain and matched DMSO vehicle concentration remain unresolved.

![Or42a: two sequential measurement rounds](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/621c89de7a51031bdc99234a202f54426f263dc5b20b8bf3bd4688997df72dc2.avif)

*Test 1 paired-round plot: plain assay buffer in round 1, test addition in round 2, each normalized to its own baseline. These are two stages of Test 1, not Test 1 versus Test 2. Plain buffer is not a documented DMSO-matched vehicle. The plot shows both individual rounds; the table supplies R and the between-well B and D contrasts.*

entries.title: Interpretation and next validation for the Or42a condition
entries.body_markdown:
The large buffer-only value H03, R = **+0.3150**, dominates the between-well comparison. Its first-round change is −0.3008 and its second-round change is +0.0142: the positive R mainly reflects subtraction of an earlier decline. For VUAA1, R = **−0.0263** becomes B = **−0.3413** and D = **−0.4004**; the other retained stimuli are also negative after both corrections.

These negative differences are useful diagnostics of control dependence, not evidence for receptor inhibition. The threshold-sensitive microscopy counts add a separate reason to check expression before interpreting a ligand panel. A repeated preparation with matched control wells would distinguish a reproducible condition effect from the influence of this single H03 reference.

The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.

Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Sources and references

The collection distinguishes these small derived attachments from the unpublished raw-data archive.

entries.title: Or42a: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or42a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 5**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or42a: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/36ebe18c-060e-4fbb-a43f-b8e673dd3b13/a61c83e58f80cd85a578d3a323b66b71f7e25bb6ad91561525edd4e5cf718620.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/ca0176abd7b0f3f03551a75f55c8a4be7e39eeedfce0c1a3492b22387406fe90.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A05 | VUAA1 | -2.57 | +36.66 | +39.23 | +39.54 | +23.53 | | D05 | Isopentyl acetate | -1.86 | -2.58 | -0.72 | -0.41 | +0.91 | | E05 | 2-Heptanone | -1.85 | -2.77 | -0.92 | -0.61 | +0.67 | | F05 | Valeric acid | -2.09 | +6.08 | +8.17 | +8.47 | +5.40 | | G05 | Pentyl acetate | -2.61 | -2.94 | -0.34 | -0.03 | +1.14 | | H05 | DMSO vehicle | -2.12 | -2.43 | -0.31 | +0.00 | +0.92 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +39.23 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -0.31 pp**. Their difference is **+39.54 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+36.66%**, while F0 changes **-2.57%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +39.23 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -0.31 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+39.54 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +23.53 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+39.54 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.

entries.title: A calcium-dependent fluorescent domain for a translational fusion
entries.body_markdown:
GCaMP6f is a genetically encoded calcium indicator described by Chen et al. [1]. Calcium-dependent changes in the calmodulin–peptide/circularly permuted GFP architecture alter green fluorescence. The team design attributes the source to Addgene plasmid #40755 [2].

The published part sequence is **1,245 bp**. It starts with `GTG`, not an initiator `ATG`, and does not end with a stop codon; this submitted fragment is intended for an in-frame fusion context. In `BBa_26E11Z80`, an upstream RSET leader supplies the translation start and the downstream linker connects it to Orco. A standalone expression design needs a suitable start context, reading frame and termination sequence.

### Why this domain

The fast GCaMP6 variant offers a literature-supported starting point for following changing calcium signals. Its performance in neuronal studies does not specify the kinetics, sensitivity or dynamic range of this Orco fusion in HEK293 cells. Our manual-addition, 12-second sampling assay cannot independently resolve channel-opening kinetics or show that indicator speed is limiting.

GCaMP fluorescence is an intensity measurement. It can change with reporter abundance, cell number, optical conditions and the cellular environment as well as calcium. Therefore, changes in signal are not automatically receptor responses. Gain should be fixed and the measurement range checked experimentally; no universal baseline percentage or saturation margin is established here.

### Functional architecture

![GCaMP6f domain within the reporter fusion](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/8ae92945f7e933b3c28f38efc407b7175d9cfe18bcd7cd80697b3a33b37566a5.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted 1,245 bp domain begins with GTG and has no terminal stop codon. The parent fusion supplies its translation start upstream and continues through the linker into Orco; this is not a standalone complete expression cassette.*

### Reading the reporter-associated evidence

The parent [BBa_26E11Z80](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80) supplies the relevant fixed-cell and kinetic observations. In its fusion-only image condition, 24/342 eligible objects were GREEN-positive at the blank-derived p99 cutoff, compared with 1/170 in the blank that also defined the cutoff. The P2 VUAA1 well A11 has R = +0.2148, B = +0.2316 and D = +0.1725. These are observations on the complete reporter–receptor construct, not calibration of free GCaMP6f.

The useful distinction for reuse is between having measurable green fluorescence and having a calibrated calcium indicator in a new context. The first is supported by the parent condition. The second would require an independent calibration of the chosen expression arrangement; these data do not determine a calcium concentration, affinity or dynamic range.

### Characterisation status

The free indicator was not measured independently. Endpoint microscopy and P2 measurements were made on constructs containing the domain and are reported on the parent fusion page. They do not determine this basic part's calcium affinity, pH response, dynamic range, maturation efficiency or performance relative to other GCaMP variants.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,245 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **EcoRI×1; PstI×2**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### References

1. Chen T-W, Wardill TJ, Sun Y, et al. Ultrasensitive fluorescent proteins for imaging neuronal activity. *Nature* 499, 295–300 (2013). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature12354
2. Addgene. pGP-CMV-GCaMP6f, plasmid #40755. https://www.addgene.org/40755/



### Additional parent-system characterization

The [parent reporter–Orco fusion](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) includes the complete Test 2 ORCO-only profile, using within-F1 change minus within-F0 drift. Its [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) distinguish this calculation from Test 1 and retain the equal-duration sensitivity result. The ORCO-only label refers to the assembled fusion-system condition; it does not establish an independent measurement of free GCaMP6f or compare alternative component designs.

entries.title: Or98a condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or98a+ORCO, with **286 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **2/286 (0.7%)**, GREEN-positive **2/286 (0.7%)**, and both-positive **2/286 (0.7%)**. Eligible objects represented 20.2% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or98a+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/f47134a04c4cb7ddd345f62e7812724c193dc9a1c3b06bb5f966cc346b37ba7c.avif)

*Or98a+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 88/286 (30.8%) | 11/286 (3.8%) |
| p99 | 2/286 (0.7%) | 2/286 (0.7%) |
| p99.5 | 0/286 (0.0%) | 2/286 (0.7%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

RED-positive counts change from 88 at p95 to 2 at p99 and zero at p99.5. GREEN-positive counts also fall from 11 to 2. This condition particularly illustrates why diffuse image brightness should not be reported as transfection efficiency or treated as a stable positive call.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A04 | VUAA1 | -0.0322 | -0.0519 | -0.0198 | -0.0039 | -0.0629 |
| D04 | 3-octanol | +0.0262 | +0.0365 | +0.0103 | +0.0262 | -0.0563 |
| E04 | benzaldehyde | +0.0032 | +0.0401 | +0.0368 | +0.0528 | -0.0766 |
| F04 | 2-heptanone | +0.0222 | +0.0391 | +0.0169 | +0.0328 | -0.0638 |
| G04 | valeric acid | +0.0304 | +0.0326 | +0.0022 | +0.0181 | -0.0265 |
| H04 | buffer only | -0.0245 | -0.0404 | -0.0159 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

B and D for the buffer row are zero by construction. Rows B (ethyl propionate) and C (isopentyl acetate) are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes; their raw data remain in the archive. Nominal VUAA1 final concentration is 50 µM in the source report, not independently verified. Final VOC molarity, numeric detector gain and matched DMSO vehicle concentration remain unresolved.

![Or98a: two sequential measurement rounds](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/8f11934fc42d9ae9b88da70c40bc528ae9cae9a97356c6c94c2dabce127ab603.avif)

*Test 1 paired-round plot: plain assay buffer in round 1, test addition in round 2, each normalized to its own baseline. These are two stages of Test 1, not Test 1 versus Test 2. Plain buffer is not a documented DMSO-matched vehicle. The plot shows both individual rounds; the table supplies R and the between-well B and D contrasts.*

entries.title: Interpretation and next validation for the Or98a condition
entries.body_markdown:
The four retained VOC rows have positive R and B, but each changes sign after the untransfected contrast is subtracted. For benzaldehyde (E04), R = **+0.0368**, B = **+0.0528**, and D = **−0.0766**. The shared biological background therefore matters even when subtracting the same-condition buffer alone leaves a positive value.

The endpoint RED count is also particularly cutoff-sensitive: 88 objects at p95, two at p99, and none at p99.5. Neither record supports a stable expression or ligand-response estimate. The 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one reference stimulus used for Or98a by Zboray et al. was absent from P2, so this screen does not directly test reproduction of that published response.

The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.
