entries.title: Or98a: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or98a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 10**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or98a: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/6a7ebea5-3d9b-4121-bbd7-fe886aff1d98/89a0619132de3845f1a4a3057e0539f4363f159e2024edacde9a64a00de7289c.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/2c7b504d5fbed3955da7a0c8952f8eac50ad3fad0192a0a2f45a799c2eb53b9f.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A10 | VUAA1 | -2.68 | +26.78 | +29.46 | +30.83 | +9.82 | | D10 | Isopentyl acetate | -1.45 | -2.45 | -1.00 | +0.37 | +0.28 | | E10 | 2-Heptanone | -1.18 | -1.91 | -0.74 | +0.63 | +0.41 | | F10 | Valeric acid | -0.92 | +0.89 | +1.81 | +3.18 | +1.08 | | G10 | Pentyl acetate | -1.64 | -2.00 | -0.36 | +1.00 | +0.66 | | H10 | DMSO vehicle | -1.11 | -2.48 | -1.37 | +0.00 | +0.31 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +29.46 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -1.37 pp**. Their difference is **+30.83 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+26.78%**, while F0 changes **-2.68%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +29.46 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -1.37 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+30.83 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +9.82 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+30.83 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.

entries.title: Or42a coding sequence for assembly into an olfactory receptor expression system
entries.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or42a subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or42a CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/598981854d287acd8c5d3fbc6a45a9f8455c462f6902a7d79b78fb96c6985333.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or42a CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0033041](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0033041.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0086052 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_523622](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_523622) |
| Reference protein length | 406 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_26Q1Q094 module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q1q094) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or42a-labelled colony plate (photograph 2, lower-right), gel D lanes 7–8, the fixed-cell **Or42a+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 03**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,221 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×4; BbsI×2**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or42a+ORCO to column 5**. The corresponding [BBa_26Q1Q094 module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q1q094#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within-F1 changes after subtraction of F0-stage drift. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) define the two time windows, percentage-point units and equal-duration sensitivity calculation.

These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.

entries.title: Or22a expression module with an independent fluorescent marker
entries.body_markdown:
This module is intended to supply the tuning receptor in a co-expression system with GCaMP6f–Orco (`BBa_26E11Z80`). The receptor and co-receptor form the expected sensing complex; the IRES drives translation of mCherry as a separate protein. Red fluorescence is an expression-associated marker, not a measurement of receptor abundance, surface localization or channel function.

The receptor's design source is recorded on its CDS page. Team records describe human codon adaptation and GenScript synthesis in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Neither enhanced expression from codon adaptation nor an optimal OR:Orco ratio has been established by a matched comparison.

### Functional architecture

![Or22a bicistronic architecture](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/ad2b346b43ee3c17f6a6d0d645b2a18b5ed64ceefaec0874c8ac6ae25f43e42e.svg)

*Design schematic, not to scale: the Or22a coding sequence is followed by EMCV IRES and mCherry. Or22a and mCherry are separate proteins; the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion is supplied by a separate co-expressed construct. Membrane localization and channel function are hypotheses to test, not observations established by the diagram.*

### Literature context

The DoOR 2.0 resource provides primary experimental provenance for Drosophila odor-response profiles. Its measurements span biological contexts and normalization methods; they should guide ligand selection rather than be treated as quantitative predictions for this HEK293 calcium assay.

The [collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156) records the tested ligand panel and its selection limits. This screen is not an exhaustive ligand profile for this receptor.

entries.title: Or22a condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or22a+ORCO, with **189 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **8/189 (4.2%)**, GREEN-positive **1/189 (0.5%)**, and both-positive **1/189 (0.5%)**. Eligible objects represented 9.9% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or22a+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/ff50a048472555b57b30ad18911814aca84e0a5ec432bda1de4e8c0aff487540.avif)

*Or22a+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 24/189 (12.7%) | 3/189 (1.6%) |
| p99 | 8/189 (4.2%) | 1/189 (0.5%) |
| p99.5 | 8/189 (4.2%) | 1/189 (0.5%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

Eight RED-positive objects and one GREEN-positive object remain at both p99 and p99.5; the one GREEN-positive object is also RED-positive at p99. This records a sparse local co-detection signal, rather than evidence that the whole culture expresses an intact sensing complex.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A05 | VUAA1 | -0.0780 | -0.0295 | +0.0485 | -0.0782 | -0.1373 |
| D05 | 3-octanol | +0.0249 | +0.0154 | -0.0094 | -0.1361 | -0.2186 |
| E05 | benzaldehyde | -0.0049 | +0.0311 | +0.0360 | -0.0906 | -0.2201 |
| F05 | 2-heptanone | +0.0043 | +0.0363 | +0.0320 | -0.0947 | -0.1913 |
| G05 | valeric acid | +0.0414 | +0.0243 | -0.0170 | -0.1437 | -0.1883 |
| H05 | buffer only | -0.0300 | +0.0966 | +0.1267 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

B and D for the buffer row are zero by construction. Rows B (ethyl propionate) and C (isopentyl acetate) are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes; their raw data remain in the archive. Nominal VUAA1 final concentration is 50 µM in the source report, not independently verified. Final VOC molarity, numeric detector gain and matched DMSO vehicle concentration remain unresolved.

![Or22a: two sequential measurement rounds](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/54ed5ad4f9a2a728ad882cd0eb19b6fedb5880fd3c87243da74ab4040b778e04.avif)

*Test 1 paired-round plot: plain assay buffer in round 1, test addition in round 2, each normalized to its own baseline. These are two stages of Test 1, not Test 1 versus Test 2. Plain buffer is not a documented DMSO-matched vehicle. The plot shows both individual rounds; the table supplies R and the between-well B and D contrasts.*

entries.title: Interpretation and next validation for the Or22a condition
entries.body_markdown:
A05 appears positive if only the between-round value is read: R = **+0.0485**. The Or22a buffer-only well H05 has the larger R = **+0.1267**, giving B = **−0.0782** and D = **−0.1373** for VUAA1. All retained stimulus B and D values are negative. This pattern is not equivalent to inhibition, because every value depends on the same single buffer reference.

The endpoint record contains only one GREEN-positive/dual-positive object at p99 among 189 eligible objects. It provides a concrete expression-associated observation, but cannot establish a sufficiently co-expressing culture for functional interpretation. The next question is whether a reproducible co-expression preparation yields stimulus changes that exceed its matched handling and vehicle controls.

The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **2,498 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **SpeI×1; PstI×2; BsmBI×1; BbsI×3**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Sources and references

- Reproducible methods: [nuclear-object analysis](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/microscopy/analyze_nuclear_objects.py) and [executed P2 methods](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/b826bffef90c-plate-p2-methods.pdf).
- Characterization tables: [microscopy condition counts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/0adc745db174-nuclear-object-per-condition.csv), [P2 well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/257ea425bbdd-plate-p2-well-summary.csv) and [P2 control contrasts](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/downloads/df638ed341f7-plate-p2-control-contrasts.csv). The collection distinguishes these small derived attachments from the unpublished raw-data archive.
- Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
- Münch D, Galizia CG. DoOR 2.0—Comprehensive Mapping of Drosophila melanogaster Odorant Responses. *Scientific Reports* 6, 21841 (2016). https://doi.org/10.1038/srep21841
- Shaner NC, Campbell RE, Steinbach PA, et al. Improved monomeric red, orange and yellow fluorescent proteins derived from Discosoma sp. red fluorescent protein. *Nature Biotechnology* 22, 1567–1572 (2004). https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt1037

entries.title: Or22a: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or22a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 3**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or22a: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/6a325ce6-70cf-4a06-89ca-764a280e1079/856f568bbabe150f87fbc6d93915e7c8a5541aaa4a221bb661b4843022782ef2.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/b2631802bb23f8571783306009096352cda5fbed67d8d7a601faf7c8fd9554f3.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A03 | VUAA1 | -2.31 | +11.13 | +13.44 | +15.10 | +9.25 | | D03 | Isopentyl acetate | -2.35 | -1.89 | +0.46 | +2.11 | +1.20 | | E03 | 2-Heptanone | -2.28 | -3.19 | -0.91 | +0.74 | +0.52 | | F03 | Valeric acid | -2.24 | -1.61 | +0.63 | +2.29 | +1.42 | | G03 | Pentyl acetate | -1.70 | -1.98 | -0.27 | +1.38 | +0.51 | | H03 | DMSO vehicle | -1.87 | -3.53 | -1.66 | +0.00 | -0.16 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +13.44 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -1.66 pp**. Their difference is **+15.10 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+11.13%**, while F0 changes **-2.31%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +13.44 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -1.66 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+15.10 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +9.25 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+15.10 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.

entries.title: Or67a coding sequence for assembly into an olfactory receptor expression system
entries.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or67a subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or67a CDS in the expression-module context](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/bf02f2c89732a0edf008fc913da29edd1eb2cfbc5eee0cc7621c973b2066ed65.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or67a CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0036009](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0036009.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0076375 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_524005](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_524005) |
| Reference protein length | 407 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_265G8CE1 module](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265g8ce1) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or67a-labelled colony plate (photograph 2, upper-left), gel D lanes 3–4, the fixed-cell **Or67a+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 06**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **1,224 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×2; BsaI×1**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### References

1. Sato K, Pellegrino M, Nakagawa T, et al. Insect olfactory receptors are heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels. *Nature* 452, 1002–1006 (2008). https://doi.org/10.1038/nature06850
2. Zboray K, Toth AV, Miskolczi TD, et al. High-throughput ligand profile characterization in novel cell lines expressing seven heterologous insect olfactory receptors for the detection of volatile plant biomarkers. *Scientific Reports* 13, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4



### Additional system-level characterization

Test 2 maps **Or67a+ORCO to column 7**. The corresponding [BBa_265G8CE1 module entry](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265g8ce1#odor-2026-10-21) gives the complete six-addition traces and within-F1 changes after subtraction of F0-stage drift. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) define the two time windows, percentage-point units and equal-duration sensitivity calculation.

These measurements belong to the labelled co-expression condition. They do not independently characterize the bare CDS, verify receptor localization or establish a ligand-specific response. The Test 1 paired-round measurements retain their distinct definition and source mapping.

entries.title: Or59b condition: endpoint fluorescence and exploratory Test 1 control contrasts
entries.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or59b+ORCO, with **230 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **38/230 (16.5%)**, GREEN-positive **3/230 (1.3%)**, and both-positive **2/230 (0.9%)**. Eligible objects represented 21.1% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or59b+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/d4968628a670277d07dd8c154212dc1d8172ea71c14152517e9aff7fffa9b17e.avif)

*Or59b+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 89/230 (38.7%) | 13/230 (5.7%) |
| p99 | 38/230 (16.5%) | 3/230 (1.3%) |
| p99.5 | 36/230 (15.7%) | 1/230 (0.4%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

The RED count remains comparatively stable from p99 to p99.5 (38 to 36), whereas GREEN-positive objects decrease from three to one. The robust red marker and sparse green signal should be distinguished when deciding which expression component to investigate next.

### Test 1: paired-round fluorescence measurements

**Assay labels.** “Round 1” and “round 2” in the older plot are the buffer and test stages of **Test 1**, not separate tests. Its R/B/D table values are dimensionless (×100 gives percentage points). The later **[Test 2 characterization](#odor-2026-10-21)** below uses the same within-F1 minus within-F0 calculation as the wiki, with S in percentage points.

One plate, one well per condition–stimulus combination; raw export headers span **10–11 October 2026**. R = ΔFtest − ΔFblank; B subtracts the same-condition buffer-only well; D additionally subtracts the same-stimulus untransfected-minus-buffer contrast. Full equations, denominators, provenance and exclusions are in [the collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156).

| Well | Addition | ΔFblank | ΔFtest | R | B | D |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A08 | VUAA1 | +0.0045 | -0.0325 | -0.0370 | -0.1019 | -0.1610 |
| D08 | 3-octanol | +0.0110 | +0.0367 | +0.0257 | -0.0392 | -0.1217 |
| E08 | benzaldehyde | -0.0118 | +0.0361 | +0.0478 | -0.0171 | -0.1465 |
| F08 | 2-heptanone | -0.0011 | +0.0344 | +0.0355 | -0.0294 | -0.1260 |
| G08 | valeric acid | +0.0242 | +0.0268 | +0.0026 | -0.0623 | -0.1069 |
| H08 | buffer only | -0.0806 | -0.0157 | +0.0649 | +0.0000 | +0.0000 |

B and D for the buffer row are zero by construction. Rows B (ethyl propionate) and C (isopentyl acetate) are excluded from retained comparisons because of reported gain changes; their raw data remain in the archive. Nominal VUAA1 final concentration is 50 µM in the source report, not independently verified. Final VOC molarity, numeric detector gain and matched DMSO vehicle concentration remain unresolved.

![Or59b: two sequential measurement rounds](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/b350a667418a1ccab1b14b86e3643f8d3960ff47af5c55d536b0be94660271dc.avif)

*Test 1 paired-round plot: plain assay buffer in round 1, test addition in round 2, each normalized to its own baseline. These are two stages of Test 1, not Test 1 versus Test 2. entries.body_markdown:
For the retained VOCs, small positive R values become negative after subtracting the same-condition buffer H08 (R = **+0.0649**). The endpoint red marker is retained in 38/230 objects at p99, whereas only three objects are GREEN-positive. The marker and the calcium-reporter domain therefore contribute different evidence. The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **2,501 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **PstI×1; BbsI×3**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Sources and references

entries.title: Or59b: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or59b+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 6**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or59b: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/1fd20db2-a481-44b8-84fd-57cbe46514c5/043374256b469877725b86f61290d1b25a661059e906341a28969a2f7d199d79.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/53f93ddc0c1ac8d3eee0bd9f6adf66e831fca32be9c2f5e178735bf34cc50db4.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A06 | VUAA1 | -1.71 | +15.71 | +17.42 | +18.71 | +12.19 | | D06 | Isopentyl acetate | -1.23 | -1.89 | -0.66 | +0.63 | +0.30 | | E06 | 2-Heptanone | -1.74 | -2.43 | -0.69 | +0.60 | +0.53 | | F06 | Valeric acid | -1.90 | +0.57 | +2.46 | +3.75 | +1.98 | | G06 | Pentyl acetate | -2.87 | -1.52 | +1.36 | +2.65 | +1.08 | | H06 | DMSO vehicle | -1.74 | -3.03 | -1.29 | +0.00 | +0.38 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +17.42 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -1.29 pp**. Their difference is **+18.71 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **+15.71%**, while F0 changes **-1.71%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +17.42 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -1.29 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+18.71 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +12.19 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+18.71 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.

entries.title: Or7a expression module with an independent fluorescent marker
entries.body_markdown:
This module is intended to supply the tuning receptor in a co-expression system with GCaMP6f–Orco (`BBa_26E11Z80`). The receptor and co-receptor form the expected sensing complex; the IRES drives translation of mCherry as a separate protein. Red fluorescence is an expression-associated marker, not a measurement of receptor abundance, surface localization or channel function.

The receptor's design source is recorded on its CDS page. Team records describe human codon adaptation and GenScript synthesis in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Neither enhanced expression from codon adaptation nor an optimal OR:Orco ratio has been established by a matched comparison.

### Functional architecture

![Or7a bicistronic architecture](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/1e5d35498251bd9b989a0ee41bd4a2a24016970ab2acf05d74c82e94b505ab1f.svg)

*Design schematic, not to scale: the Or7a coding sequence is followed by EMCV IRES and mCherry. Or7a and mCherry are separate proteins; the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion is supplied by a separate co-expressed construct. Membrane localization and channel function are hypotheses to test, not observations established by the diagram.*

### Literature context

The stable-cell study of Zboray et al. included Or7a but did not obtain responses to its tested VOC panel. That result is specific to their system; it does not establish a universal absence of Or7a ligand responses.

The [collection](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156) records the tested ligand panel and its selection limits. This screen is not an exhaustive ligand profile for this receptor.

entries.title: Interpretation and next validation for the Or7a condition
entries.body_markdown:
The most informative retained odorant well is F01 (2-heptanone): R = **+0.1835**, B = **+0.2141**, and D = **+0.1176**. Inspection of the two rounds explains why this is not simply an 18.35% ligand-evoked rise: the buffer-round change is −0.1637, while the test-round change is only +0.0198. The positive contrast remains after the untransfected reference, but part of its magnitude comes from the earlier decline. The fusion-only 2-heptanone well also has D = +0.1056, so the sign is not specific to the Or7a module.

VUAA1 gives R = −0.0549 and D = −0.0833 in A01, with buffer reference H01 at R = −0.0307. Together with the sparse GREEN-positive endpoint count, these records motivate separating expression of the fusion from tuning-receptor ligand selection. They do not establish a nonfunctional Or7a protein: the microscopy and P2 preparations are not batch-linked, and P2 does not contain a validated concentration-response series.

The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **2,546 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **EcoRI×1; PstI×3; BsmBI×1; BbsI×3**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.

### Sources and references

The collection distinguishes these small derived attachments from the unpublished raw-data archive.

entries.title: Or7a: Test 2 fluorescence dynamics with baseline-drift subtraction
entries.body_markdown: ### Assay context Test 2 measures **the Or7a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 1**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or7a: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/2dcafb6a-80c0-4d8f-9622-eea1dac117c9/56cf47bdea01ccde3c595c61728a375d081b7a1fddf3a8353e50e563c78f406d.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF1 − ΔF0, in percentage points (pp), using the observed F1 change over 168 s and F0 change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* [Full within-acquisition F0/F1 time courses](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/58847a0862417c13be5ffc3727f226522149624fa00b2c36d06d7537f4e3e183.avif). ΔF0 = 100 × (last F0 / first F0 − 1); ΔF1 = 100 × (last F1 / first F1 − 1). **S = ΔF1 − ΔF0**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of F1 and the full 48 s of F0; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF0 (%) · 48 s | ΔF1 (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A01 | VUAA1 | -1.87 | -1.47 | +0.40 | +2.19 | +1.13 | | D01 | Isopentyl acetate | -1.96 | -3.06 | -1.10 | +0.69 | +0.05 | | E01 | 2-Heptanone | -1.62 | -2.99 | -1.37 | +0.42 | -0.02 | | F01 | Valeric acid | -2.44 | -2.10 | +0.34 | +2.13 | +1.06 | | G01 | Pentyl acetate | -1.58 | -2.62 | -1.04 | +0.75 | +0.36 | | H01 | DMSO vehicle | -0.26 | -2.05 | -1.79 | +0.00 | -0.70 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +0.40 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -1.79 pp**. Their difference is **+2.19 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. The small +2.19 pp reference denominator makes Or7a ratios particularly sensitive to small well differences. For VUAA1, the within-F1 change is **-1.47%**, while F0 changes **-1.87%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +0.40 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -1.79 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+2.19 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +1.13 pp**. S answers whether the recorded F1 trajectory changes more than the recorded F0 trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean F1 level with the preceding mean F0 level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising F1 trace and a lower F1 mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the [audit summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/c324535fe528-well-summary.csv) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means F1 changes more, or decreases less, than F0; it need not imply a raw F1 increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+2.19 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. This is the smallest reference in the displayed panel: valeric acid gives +2.13 pp / +2.19 pp = **0.972**. Its high relative value must be read beside the small absolute reference; the VUAA1 F1 trajectory itself decreases. Attachments: [corrected 72-well summary](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/37cf3f799488-change-summary.csv), [import provenance](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts-data/8de9b0e74dac-import-manifest.json) and [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods). Dates, raw identifiers and unmodified source measurements remain in the provenance record.
